Top Republicans were reportedly not given any warning that President Donald Trump would propose sending $5,000 checks to Americans after the midterms, a plan they reportedly have doubts will ever become reality.

Those out of the loop about the proposal included Senate Majority Leader John Thune, The Washington Sun reported.

“It’s not going to happen,” a GOP aide told the outlet, warning that a wave of checks could drive inflation.

Republican Rep. Chip Roy, who criticized the plan on X as a form of unneeded government “dependency,” told the Sun he was not given advance notice of the plan.

The Independent has contacted Thune and the White House for comment.

open image in gallery Top Republicans were reportedly surprised by the president’s plan to send $5,000 checks to Americans after the midterms ( Getty )

During his speech on Wednesday at the Republican midterm convention in Texas, President Trump said the administration would pay American adults $5,000 checks if voters helped the GOP retain its majority in Congress.

“So if the Republicans win, you win with us, and you get $5,000,” Trump said. “It will be called the Trump Dividend.”

Since then, the White House has offered few details about the plan, including how it would be funded or why the government wouldn’t send checks to Americans now if it had the money.

The president has linked the money with tariff revenues.

“Because the Democrats can’t do it. Because with them, it’s negative growth. With us, it’s so positive,” Trump told Fox News after the speech. “So, we’re taking in $21 trillion. No country has ever taken in anywhere near that. It’s four or five times higher than the next one. All because of that beautiful word you and I love more than most others, tariffs.”

In a separate interview with CBS Texas, the president said he didn’t think he needed lawmakers’ approval for the payouts, despite the Constitution vesting Congress with the power to collect taxes and direct federal spending.

“Well, we think not,” Trump said. “I think they will do it if we needed it. But we think not.”

open image in gallery Senate Majority Leader John Thune was reportedly among those not told about the plan ahead of time ( AFP/Getty )

During the pandemic, the Biden administration also sent checks to Americans, though these were funded by legislation.

Some Republicans said they were eager to pass the president’s payment plan.

“I will get a bill ready so that we can get the Trump Dividend passed immediately after the November 3rd election … because Republicans (and America) will win!” Senator Bernie Moreno of Ohio wrote on X after the speech.

“President Trump has consistently proven his doubters wrong, drawing a clear contrast with the Democrats’ record of historic inflation, unfettered illegal immigration, skyrocketing crime, and weakness on the world stage,” White House spokesman Davis Ingle previously told The Independent in a statement when asked about the details of the plan.

During his speech on Wednesday, the president said the checks were contingent on voters delivering a Republican majority in the midterms.

open image in gallery Some Republicans are reportedly skeptical the $5,000 check plan will move forward, given the possibility it could drive inflation ( AFP/Getty )

“So if the Republicans win, you win with us, and you get $5,000,” Trump said during his remarks.

Critics accused the president of attempting to buy support ahead of November.

Trump has repeatedly floated payments for Americans that have never arrived, including $2,000 checks tied to tariff income, $5,000 checks from DOGE savings and federal funds for healthcare spending. During the Wednesday night speech, Trump compared the payout to the administration’s $1,776 “Warrior Dividend” checks for American military service members.

News.title: Rampant Manchester United win first Champions League game in 1,003 days
News.content:
This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

United’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

News.title: Stephen Fleming learning nothing from rout of Pakistan
News.content:
Stephen Fleming arrives next week to start his job as England Test coach and his first task will be to apply his famously meticulous mind to assess a whitewash of Pakistan.

England are not quite there yet. Rain denied them a two-day win at Edgbaston, Pakistan finishing 52 for two, another 268 behind after England’s 453 all out.

But when the game does finish, and England complete a rout that started with Ollie Robinson taking a wicket with the first ball of the series, it will be time to look ahead to a proper challenge: a three-match series against Test champions South Africa over Christmas.

That series will give Fleming a much better guide to where his team stand in the lead-up to the Ashes summer. This one is less clearcut. Fleming has been in daily contact with Joe Root and will lean heavily on him and Marcus North. the national selector, for insight, but drawing definitive conclusions is impossible because of the lack of competitive cricket.

A quartet of quicks has emerged, led by Robinson, whose 21 wickets in the series at 6.6 look like a misprint. A double-wicket maiden to start Pakistan’s second innings would normally be headline-grabbing stuff. This time it felt almost predictable, even disappointing for those wanting to see some sort of contest.

News.title: West Nile virus hits Europe as temperatures climb
News.content:
“The future looks rosy for West Nile virus and other mosquito-borne viruses that follow it to the New World,” wrote the science writer Carl Zimmer in his 2011 book ‘Planet of Viruses’.

“That’s because the future is going to be warm and wet.”

More than a decade on, and after a record-setting hot summer, Mr Zimmer’s prediction has come to pass: the mosquito-borne disease, once confined mostly to the warmest parts of Africa, has become firmly entrenched in Europe, experts have warned.

At least 1,086 locally acquired cases of West Nile virus have been recorded across the continent over the last three months, as mosquitoes continue their slow march northwards.

The insects – which are cold-blooded – need warm weather to accelerate their life cycles and survive long enough to spread disease.

Across July and August, countries including Italy, Spain and France recorded West Nile cases in previously unaffected regions and cities, while others, including the Netherlands, recorded their first deaths from the virus this summer.

“I don’t think there are any more ‘tropical viruses’... the geographic barrier of these viruses no longer exists because of climate change,” said Dr Krishanthi Subramaniam, a microbiology lecturer at the University of Liverpool.

News.title: Britain pioneers new dried blood products for the modern battlefield
News.content:
A powdered blood product that can be mixed with water and used in minutes could help solve the challenges of treating severely wounded soldiers on hard-to-reach battlefields.

Britain is rethinking how to get blood to soldiers on the frontline, in the latest sign that the war in Ukraine has forced Western militaries to reconsider assumptions about modern combat medicine that had held since Iraq and Afghanistan.

The product, known as “spray-dried plasma”, is made by turning liquid plasma – the clotting-rich component of blood – into a stable powder that can be stored at room temperature for years before being rehydrated with water when needed.

“Plasma is vital for saving soldiers in war zones,” said Dr Ian Nesbitt, a former military anaesthetist and Faculty Lead for Anaesthesia at the David Nott Foundation, which trains doctors working in conflict zones.

“It helps blood clot when someone is injured. But in war zones, getting plasma to soldiers is incredibly complicated. It’s actually the logistics of it that are a real problem in maintaining a reliable supply of fresh frozen plasma for acutely injured patients.”

The NHS and the UK Ministry of Defence signed a strategic partnership this summer to jointly develop new blood products for frontline soldiers, focusing on dried plasma.

The agreement formalises work under way with a biotechnology company called Velico Medical. If successful, it will be used in future battlefields like the one in Ukraine.

“The war in Ukraine has woken up all countries, not just the UK,” Professor Renata Gomes, Chief Scientific Officer at NHS Blood and Transplant (NHSBT), told The Telegraph.

News.title: Mosquitoes are evolving to evade bed nets – but there may be a solution
News.content:
In Papua’s low-lying mangrove swamps and dense tropical rainforests, mosquitoes have always got to work early.

Here, the disease-ridden insects begin feeding in the early evening as people socialise and children play. It’s a characteristic that’s hampered malaria control efforts, because it has rendered bed nets less effective. People are bitten before they climb under the netting to sleep.

It’s also part of the reason that Indonesian Papua remains one of Asia’s most persistent malaria hotspots. Last year, cases across the country jumped by 30 per cent, to 706,000 new infections. The vast majority, roughly 90 per cent, were reported in Papua’s six provinces.

The same pattern is now emerging in parts of sub-Saharan Africa, where mosquitoes used to bite mostly at night and where the rollout of insecticide-treated bed nets is estimated to have averted 450 million malaria cases between 2000 and 2015, according to modelling in Nature journal.

A number of studies suggest mosquitoes in Africa are evolving in response to the mass rollout of bed nets, biting earlier in the evening, or later in the morning. In some cases, species which already did this have become more dominant, while others are adapting their habits.

“We’re battling evolution. And right now, we’re losing,” said Prof Neil Lobo, a research professor in the Eck Institute for Global Health at the University of Notre Dame.

“Mosquitoes are adapting. They’re biting outdoors, they’re biting earlier in the evening when people aren’t under their nets, and they’re becoming resistant to the insecticides we use. So we’re reaching the limits of what bed nets alone can do,” he told The Telegraph.

But there may be a solution.

News.title: Palmer and Rogers complete 12-minute rescue mission to save Chelsea
News.content:
Xabi Alonso needed the cavalry – and referee Jarred Gillett – to stop Chelsea making a quick exit from the Carabao Cup and, boy, did they come up trumps for him.

Chelsea had looked to be heading out of the competition shortly after half-time, but, in Cole Palmer and Morgan Rogers, Alonso has a cheat code that is capable of masking even the worst defending.

Alonso’s side have shared 26 goals in the five games they have played this season. It has certainly been an entertaining start by Chelsea’s latest manager.

Palmer, Rogers and Pedro Neto stepped off the substitutes’ bench to complete a stunning rescue mission against Leeds United. Palmer scored twice, Neto once and Rogers helped himself to at least a hat-trick of assists. He claimed it was four, but the record books may say three.

When it was announced Palmer had been awarded the player of the match, Rogers responded by saying: “Mate, I got four assists. I can’t believe that! That’s mental. He scored a pen!”

News.title: Martin Odegaard bails out comically wasteful Arsenal
News.content:
In five matches this season, Odegaard has already scored four goals. That is three more than he managed in the whole of last season. The Arsenal captain is fit again and he is flowing. As ever, when Odegaard flows, Arsenal flow.

“That’s what we need, the players with that mindset to decide the game and play with that personality,” said Mikel Arteta. “He has got that edge. He’s getting into those positions much more in recent games.”

In the end it was a thoroughly deserved victory for the Premier League side, who were superior to Napoli in every department. Were it not for their comically bad finishing, they would have guaranteed the result long before Odegaard’s 75th-minute strike.

Their expected goals figure suggested they should have scored more than four goals, compared to Napoli’s 0.22. In total, they registered 26 shots – the most of any Arsenal team on record in a single Champions League match, and the most on record a Napoli team has ever faced.

“With the amount of chances we generated, the scoreline has to reflect a very different result,” said Arteta. “The number of players that got into this situation, the amount of situations that we generated in various ways was something that pleased me a lot.”

Sports.title: Man City ace Donnarumma ‘bound and hit’ when robbers raided flat… as judge suspends first day of ‘catastrophic’ trial
Sports.content:
STAR'S TERROR Man City ace Donnarumma ‘bound and hit’ when robbers raided flat… as judge suspends first day of ‘catastrophic’ trial

MAN City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma was beaten, tied up and threatened with a knife by robbers who broke into his flat in Paris, a court heard.

His pregnant girlfriend Alessia Elefante was also in the home when the suspects allegedly broke in and stole £430,000 worth of loot.



The horrifying home invasion unfolded back in 2023 – but has only just gone to trial.

Insults and swearwords richocheted through the courtroom in scenes the presiding judge has called “catastrophic”.



The judge expelled defendents Ilyas Kherbouch and Khyan “Kiki” Mamouni and booted out a family member before suspending the trial shortly after 9:20pm.

Both men were thrown from the courtroom after repeated rows as Kherbouch shouted: “I don’t give a s**t”.

Kherbouch, 21, and Mamouni, 22, are on trial for allegedly masterminding the Paris flat raid from their prison cells.

Donnarumma and his pregnant girlfriend Alessia had been asleep when four men allegedly smashed the windows into their flat back on July 21, 2023, a Paris court was told today.

The goalkeeper said he woke up to a man saying “shhh” before hitting him in the face with a knuckle duster, according to bombshell court docs.

The suspected thug then threatened him with a knife and shouted “the watches, the watches”, recounted the goalkeeper in his witness statement.



Terrified, Donnarumma said he “showed him the one on the dressing table, an Audemars Piguet”.

Piguet watches are worth up to hundreds of thousands of pounds.

Alessia Elefante, who is now married to Donnarumma, told cops she was also woken up and threatened by the suspected robbers.



Alleged gangmembers shouted at her for money and watches as she scrambled to give them €2,000 in cash, a Cartier watch and jewellery.

The robbers also demanded the code for a safe in the flat – but Alessia said she did not know it and claimed it was empty.

“They got angry thinking that I was lying”, she recounted to investigators.

“They pulled me by the hair and one of them hit me on the thighs. I said I was pregnant but they continued.”

The gang eventually escaped with cash, watches, luxury handbags and the keys to a Mercedes and a Lamborghini.



Criminal mastermind Ilyas Kherbouch, 21, is accused of co-ordinating the break-in from his prison cell.

The Gen Z gang leader is serving seven years for robbing Michelin star chef Simone Zanoni.

The fiend managed to escape jail in March – only to be caught again after 13 days on the run. He denies involvement in the attack on Donnarumma and Elefante.



A second man called Khyan Mamouni, 22, nicknamed Kiki, has also been accused of masterminding the attack from behind bars – but he denies the charges.

Cops believe four men used a ladder to climb onto the rook before lowering down onto the balcony and smashing in through the windows.

Moktar Diop, 24, has admitted to breaking in to the footballer and his partner’s home but denies taking part in any violence.

A fourth suspect previously confessed to taking part in the raid but died by suicide in prison in 2024.

In July two men – aged 18 at the time of the robbery – were sentenced to three and four years in prison.

Sports.title: Jamal Musiala scores in first start since terrifyingly collapsing twice in pre-season due and unveils new celebration
Sports.content:
JAMAL MUSIALA scored on his first start for Bayern Munich since his terrifying collapses in pre-season.

The German star collapsed twice on the pitch within days before the 2026/27 Bundesliga campaign started.

Musiala, 23, was diagnosed with a “neurological dysfunction” that caused “absence seizures” – but said it was “temporary and easily treatable”.



He made his first start since the horrifying moments in the Champions League fixture against Bodo/Glimt.



And the midfielder made his time on the pitch count as he scored Bayern’s opening goal early in the second half.

Musiala turned well in the box before lashing home a powerful effort to find the net.

After wheeling away in joy, he then unveiled a brand new celebration.

He appeared to look to the stands and repeatedly pointed to the side of his head.

Musiala was then joined by team-mates Aleksandar Pavlovic, Harry Kane, Dayot Upamecano and Alphonso Davies.

He then took a moment with Davies as they shook hands in continuing celebrations.

Musiala’s collapses against Leipzig and Heidenheim – the latter just eight minutes after coming on as a sub – were absence seizures, formerly known as petit-mal seizures, which are a type of epileptic seizure.



Typically diagnosed during childhood, they are caused by a temporary neurological lapse where the brain pauses electric signals.

Davies was one of the Bayern players to speak about the incidents involving Musiala.

He said: “These two incidents broke my heart.

“The doctors are doing everything they can to help him through this situation.

“The best thing we can do as a team is give him positive energy so that he can keep a clear head and fight his way through it.



“We’ll support Jamal, not just as a player, but as a person. We have to support him as a friend, like a brother.”

Musiala’s goal kick-started Bayern’s Champions League campaign as they went on to score four more to claim a statement victory.



Kane netted the club’s second before a brace from Michael Olise and a goal from Davies.

Manager Vincent Kompany spoke about Musiala after the game and hailed the star for seizing his moment.

He said: “I think I was just as happy as the people here in the stadium, and probably many more watching on TV.

“We knew this moment would come, but you can’t predict it – it just has to happen.

“And then it was also a really important goal. For Jamal, of course, this is fantastic.



“Now I hope the focus shifts back to his performance. Everything else is part of his life; he knows how to handle it, and he has our full support.

“Of course, performance is what ultimately counts. But I also want to work with good people and enjoy coming to work myself.

“We support Jamal when things are difficult – just like any other player.



“If Jamal’s focus is solely on his athletic performance, I’m not worried in the long run.

“That’s another reason why it was a successful evening for us.”

Sports.title: Three things we learned from Man Utd’s win over Sabah as Sesko makes his case but star looks haunted by Amorim claim
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED have made a strong return to the Champions League with a 4-0 win over Sabah.

Michael Carrick‘s team dominated their Azerbaijani rivals with Matheus Cunha handing the side the lead after 27 minutes.



Captain Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko extended United‘s lead in the minutes just before half-time.

Lisandro Martinez then added a fourth midway through the second half to send the Champions League debutants away empty-handed.



DEFENSIVE DECISIONS

MANCHESTER UNITED boss Michael Carrick made three changes to the back four, clearly with Sunday’s derby in mind.

Leny Yoro, in his first start of the season, attempted to impose himself in the first minutes with an aggressive press that United supporters appreciated.

Yoro is into his third season at Old Trafford and, as he approaches his 21st birthday, also has to come of age at the club with the 33-year-old Harry Maguire his competitor. The free header for Joy-Lance Mickels at 1-0 highlighted French centre-back Yoro’s naivety.

Maguire, the de facto vice-captain, has been a first-teamer all calendar year — and will continue to be.



Patrick Dorgu started at left-back for the first time under Carrick. For someone signed on the strength of his performances in that position, the role looked alien to him.

The Denmark international, 21, appeared devoid of confidence until his classy clipped cross that Matheus Cunha turned in.

Before that, Dorgu had performed as though haunted by former Red Devils chief Ruben Amorim’s assertion last season he is prone to “anxiousness”.

Amorim belatedly realised he is better further forward — and Carrick knows that, too.

TIELEMANS CAN BE KEY MAN

YOURI TIELEMANS’ inclusion went to plan.



The Belgian midfielder admitted his body “switched off” during the World Cup amid the time-zone changes, air miles and matches.

The prospect of starting him in games less than 72 hours apart was risky, particularly against a fresher Manchester City midfield bolstered at a cost of £322million.

It was just as well United were 3-0 up at half-time, when Tielemans earned a breather.

His perceptive assist for Bruno Fernandes to score goal No 2 has likely protected his place.

But for the second game running on home soil, Kobbie Mainoo was the best player.



His defence-splitting lob for Fernandes was something the United captain would be proud of, and the home fans were on their feet to applaud the England midfielder when he was substituted

The Red Devils’ resurgence last season started not just with Carrick in the dugout against City but with Mainoo back in the starting XI.

How Tielemans complements him against City’s costly trio will be pivotal.

SESKO MAKES HIS CASE

CARRICK had likely settled on his XI for the derby before the Champions League anthem was played.

The recalled quartet, which also included Noussair Mazraoui, were up against it to ensure they kept their place for the City clash.



Benjamin Sesko was caught between a rock and a hard place.

He is an out-and-out No 9 but Carrick had played strikerless sides in 13 out of 20 games before the Sabah clash.

Sesko is developing into a goalscorer, though. He made it two goals in two games and has 12 in 2026. Eventually, he has to start leading the line in the Prem.

Sesko set his sights on adding to his tally against Manchester City this weekend as he said: “It was a perfect night for everyone, especially the fans.

“It means a lot to them when they see so many goals and gives us more motivation for Sunday.



“The confidence boost we’ll take is a big one but now we have to recover and focus on the derby.”

Sesko was making his first start of the season but eased onto Bryan Mbeumo’s pass to round the Sabah keeper and find the empty net.

He added: “I saw the keeper was rushing out so it was a great opportunity to take the ball away from him, and make the goal a little bit easier.

“The great thing was that we had four different scorers. It’s important when you know that everybody can score goals, especially as we have so many games to play this season.”

Sports.title: ‘What do you mean?’ – Champions League star’s stunned reaction after being told manager resigned in post-match interview
Sports.content:
CHAMPIONS LEAGUE star Archie Brown was left stunned after being told his manager has just resigned in his post-match interview.

Fenerbahce manager Ismail Kartal shocked reporters as he announced his resignation from his position after the 1-1 draw with Roma.



The Turkish side earned a point against the Italian giants with Brown netting the equaliser after Bryan Cristante opened the scoring.

Despite his side coming from behind to rescue a point in the UCL league phase, Kartel, 65, resigned as manager.



The Turkish coach had only been in charge for three months in what was his FOURTH spell at the club.

Brown, 24, was informed of the news as he was set to begin talking to reporters himself.



The Birmingham-born full-back was visibly stunned as he was told by a member of club staff.

The staff member said: “In the press conference, Ismail Kartal resigned.”

Brown replied: “What do you mean resigned? As what? As coach?

“He is not the coach anymore? He said this just now?



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

“I did not know about this.”

Brown was named the Player of the Match for his performance at the Chobani Stadium.

He added: “I am very happy, it was an important goal. I think we deserved a goal to be honest.

“In the second half I think we dominated the majority and we had a lot of chances and we probably should have won.

“But we go on to the next and try to get three points.”



Kartal revealed that he would be stepping down and claimed that the decision was made “as a team”.

He said: “I am resigning from my position while there is still time. I am resigning with the understanding that I will never return.

“I have been here for three months. From the beginning of the season until today, the training sessions and camps I conducted with my players



“Our president and managers tried to help us in every way.

“Those were wonderful days. As of this evening, I congratulate my players and I am resigning from my position.

“Therefore, I would like to thank all my fans, media members, staff, and fellow players who have supported me until today.

“I made this decision to pave the way for my club. We made this decision together as a team.”

Fenerbahce President Aziz Yildirim has claimed that Kartal will remain as the head coach despite his resignation.



He said: “None of us knew about the resignation decision,” Yildirim told reporters after the match.

“Ismail Kartal remains in charge. But the entire Fenerbahce community should stand behind the coach.”

Yildirim also claimed that Kartal’s decision was due to a bottle being thrown at his head.

Sports.title: Man Utd ratings: Mainoo is best player for second game running at Old Trafford but Mazraoui won’t dislodge dubious Dalot
Sports.content:
MANCHESTER UNITED cruised to a 4-0 romp over Sabah in their first Champions League clash of the season.

Michael Carrick‘s team were dominant throughout and went three goals up before half time through Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko.



Lisandro Martinez then made it four in the second half to give United a comfortable evening and a thumping start back in Europe.

SunSport’s Samuel Luckhurst gave his verdict on the players at Old Trafford.



Senne Lammens – 6

Had next to nothing to do but Joy-Lance Mickels ought to have forced him into a save with a free header at 1-0.

A much-needed calm night between the sticks for Lammens after his poorest performance for United at Everton.

Noussair Mazraoui – 6

Did not do enough to dislodge the dubious Diogo Dalot for Sunday’s derby.

Signs of ring-rust still evident after the World Cup and Mazraoui remains lacking in the final third, where Bryan Mbeumo was without a foil.



Leny Yoro – 7

Made his first start of the season and attempted to impose himself early on.

Mickels’ chance highlighted how gettable United are, however many changes they make to their defence and Yoro will be back on the bench against City.

Lisandro Martinez – 7

The only defender not given a breather after the draw with Everton, Martinez offered continuity and remained calm amid the odd charge from Kaheem Parris.

Scored on the rebound and, like Lammens, Martinez should benefit from a largely stress-free evening.

Patrick Dorgu – 6

Started at left back for the first time under Carrick. For someone signed on the strength of his form at left back for Lecce, the role looked alien to him.



Made clumsy errors and looked to have lost confidence before he rallied to cross for Matheus Cunha’s opening goal.

Kobbie Mainoo – 8

United’s best player for the second game running at Old Trafford. Played a defence-splitting lob that Bruno Fernandes wasted when he failed to find Benjamin Sesko.

Mainoo was authoritative and consistent from start to finish.



Youri Tielemans – 7

Earned himself a second-half breather after showing good awareness to tee up Bruno Fernandes to make it 2-0.

This was Tielemans’ most creative performance, which is the least he should offer against Champions League newbies.

Bryan Mbeumo – 6

Not on the scoresheet this time but heavily involved in United’s countless attacks.

Probed regularly with his runs into the penalty area before he made way in the second half.

Matheus Cunha – 7

Cunha was back on the wing and back on the scoresheet with his first goal of the season on the day he was dropped from the Brazil squad. Came close to a second with a low strike.



On this evidence, if Carrick opts for the strikerless side against City, then they would better be served with Cunha operating off the left.

Bruno Fernandes – 7

Should have assisted Benjamin Sesko before he steered in United’s second goal to all but kill the contest.

Fernandes was never going to sit out United’s return to the Champions League and Brighton in the League Cup next week may be the time to rest him.



Benjamin Sesko – 7

Urgent on his first start since May 3 and would have had a tap-in if Fernandes had angled his square pass more accurately.

Plugged away and scored coolly just before half-time to make it two goals in two games. Has to start at weekends sooner, rather than later.

Subs

Mason Mount – 6

Made his first appearance in over a month as a second-half substitute.



Occupied a central midfield role – where he is bound to play more often when fit – to hone his match fitness.

Joshua Zirkzee – 6

His flick was kept out but converted by Martinez on the rebound.

Andrey Santos – 6

Got a run-out.

Made his European debut.

Harry Amass – 6

Came on for first United appearance since May 2025.

Sports.title: Man Utd 4 Sabah 0: Carrick’s changed side breeze past minnows for first Champions League win in nearly three years
Sports.content:
MICHAEL CARRICK was punching the air before half-time, a winning start to his first full Champions League campaign already assured.

The perfect night for United, with early goals for Matheus Cunha, skipper Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko, the Euro rookies from Azerbaijan sent packing with the minimum of fuss, completed by Lisandro Martinez’ comic fourth.



After three years as outsiders while others dined at the High Table, this was an enjoyable light evening meal.

But while the Old Trafford fans enjoyed their return to the Euro elite, nobody was fooled.



The game that actually matters this week is still to come.

Beat City in the derby on Sunday, and all will seem well, the manager bolstered, faith growing.

Lose, and the clouds of doubt will return, black and foreboding.

Tonight there were no beads of worried sweat on Carrick’s brow.

What was supposed to be a mismatch against the minnows from the shores of the Caspian Sea, turned into exactly that as United completed a clean sweep of Prem wins in the opening week of the competition.

It may have taken nearly half an hour for United to make their physical domination count.



SUN VEGAS WELCOME OFFER: GET UP TO £100 BONUS

Even then, Kobbie Mainoo was able to glide through the game, positionally sound and passing with intelligence, while Youri Tielemans looked a class act alongside him.

And once Cunha, snubbed by Brazil boss Carlo Ancelotti as one of the casualties of the World Cup flop, scored his first of the season, converting Patrick Dorgu’s cross, the only question was the margin of victory.

Sabah boss Valdas Dambrauskas funded the start of his coaching career with his £725 winnings on the Lithuanian version of “Who Wants to be a Millionaire?”

He must have felt like phoning a friend for help as the quickfire double from Bruno and Sesko just before the interval took the game out of sight.

No surprise really. With the exception of Mainoo – their best performer – every one of Carrick’s starting team had cost more than the entire Sabah side.



United were bigger, stronger, fitter and simply better.

While fleet-footed Jamaican Kaheem Parris did make things uncomfortable for Dorgu, whose limitations again highlighted the folly of not buying a proper back-up for the rested Luke Shaw, it was never going to matter.

Early sighters for Cunha and Nousair Mazraoui had signposted Sabah’s frailties on the flanks, after Carrick resisted the urge to make wholesale changes ahead of Sunday’s derby showdown.

United, though, were guilty of over-elaboration, briefly raising the hopes of the handful of travelling fans in the Sabah ranks.



That was summed up when Mainoo’s delightful scoop forward found the galloping Bruno, who failed to find the unmarked Sesko, making his first start of the season with Marcus Rashford benched.

But the breakthrough came on 27 minutes, after the Azerbaijan side coughed up the ball in midfield.

The passing was swift and sharp, Bryan Mbeumo, Sesko and then Bruno combining to feed Dorgu, with Cunha escaping his alleged marker to side-foot home from six yards.

Shelling peas would have been harder, as the muted response of the home fans acknowledged. It didn’t.

And although Rwandan striker Joy-Lance Mickels should have scored with a back post header from Parris’ deflected cross, it was over by half-time.



Tielemans was involved twice in the first, instigating the move and then spinning from Cunha’s pass to allow Bruno to slide home.

Then when Mbeumo, in off the right, saw the space in behind, Sesko was able to run through unchallenged, round the keeper and pass into the net for his second in as many matches.

It was a calm finish for the Slovenian, who had earlier gone close with a back to goal volley after Tielemans’ angled pass had picked out Dorgu in space again.



The slight surprise was that Carrick waited until beyond the hour mark to make more than the one change, which has seen Mason Mount on for Tielemans at the interval.

Cunha, spinning to fire from the edge of the box, and soon afterwards Bruno, both tested Sabah keeper Stas Pokalitov.

There was a ripple of applause when Mainoo was given a deserved breather, Andrey Santos on, while Joshua Zirkzee – who was almost an Everton player last week – came on for Sesko.

Zirkzee was involved in the fourth, his back heel after Bruno’s lob-wedge free-kick eventually teeing up Martinez for a tap-in, mainly due to the Sabah keeper completely losing his bearing as the ball dribbled between his legs.

Rashford was being held back for the big one at the weekend as Carrick instead sent on youngsters Harry Amass and Shea Lacey.

That will, for sure, be a far tougher test of the manager and his players.

For now, though, the mood is positive. We will see soon for how much longer.

Sports.title: Tottenham and Bournemouth came close to signing LaLiga boss praised by Jose Mourinho, Luis Enrique and Diego Simeone
Sports.content:
TOTTENHAM and Bournemouth almost landed former Real Sociedad manager Imanol Alguacil after he played the “best football” in LaLiga.

Alguacil, 55, spent seven years in charge of Sociedad where he won Copa del Rey in 2020 – the club’s first trophy in 34 years – and took them from 15th place to the Last 16 of the Champions League and Europa League.



Under the Basque head coach, the Spanish outfit played highly entertaining football and was also credited for building the third best defence in LaLiga for several years.

That led to praise from some of the best managers in the world, such as Real Madrid‘s Jose Mourinho, Paris Saint-Germain’s Luis Enrique and Atletico Madrid’s Diego Simeone.



And SunSport can reveal Tottenham and Bournemouth tried to sign the Spanish tactician after he left Anoeta in 2025.

Spurs explored the possibility of landing Alguacil in May 2025 before hiring Thomas Frank and suffering their worst ever Premier League campaign that saw them just avoiding relegation.

Bayer Leverkusen were also interested during that time as they saw him as Xabi Alonso‘s potential replacement, while Sevilla and Porto eyed him as well.

SunSport can confirm a report from Olympiacos Roundtable claiming the Cherries then kept tabs on the Sociedad legend, who also spent eight years with the club as a player in the 90s after rising through the ranks in the academy, last summer.



Bournemouth identified him as the ideal replacement for Andoni Iraola after he announced his departure in April.

In fact, Alguacil is undefeated in all of his six matches against Iraola, 44, – who took over at Liverpool – as he beat the ex-Mirandes and Rayo Vallecano boss five times.

BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

However, SunSport understand the timing wasn’t right for the manager and Bournemouth went with Marco Rose.

The Premier League duo were especially impressed with his work developing stars like Martin Zubimendi, Mikel Merino, Mikel Oyarzabal, Alexander Isak and Robin Le Normand.

Alguacil had been a free agent since leaving Saudi Arabian outfit Al-Shabab in February.



But he has now found a new club in Olympiacos, who have just shockingly parted ways with legendary boss Jose Luis Mendilibar.

Alguacil’s record of 153 wins and 95 losses in 330 matches at Sociedad saw Mourinho, 63, admitting he struggled to find a weakness in his team after facing him as Roma manager.

The ex-Manchester United and Chelsea boss said: “It’s difficult to find weaknesses in Real Sociedad. Imanol is a very good coach; he has a very well-prepared team.



“In addition to the quality they have, they are also capable of changing systems from one match to another or even during the same game.”

Enrique, 56, stated Sociedad played the most impressive football in all of LaLiga under Alguacil, whom he faced as PSG boss.

The back-to-back European champion said: “What a great team, what a way to compete!

“They are wonderful. I’ll tell you something: Real Sociedad is the Spanish team that plays the best football, without any doubt. Imanol Alguacil deserves congratulations.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

And Simeone, 56, praised Alguacil for establishing a sense of identity at Sociedad, whom he led to fourth place in LaLiga three years ago – the club’s highest finish in a decade.



The Argentinean tactician, who lost three times to the Spaniard, said: “He has done an enormous and spectacular job since taking charge of the team. He has a clearly defined identity and it’s a pleasure to watch them play.”

Sports.title: 'A great sporting ticket' - US Open chief vows to keep day, night session format
Sports.content:
US Open chief Craig Tiley has told Sky Sports Tennis he plans on keeping two matches during the day and two at night at Flushing Meadows in 2027.

Tiley, who took the helm as new CEO of USTA earlier this year after leading Tennis Australia since 2013, says he has no plans for any changes to the schedule.

It comes after Ben Shelton's five-set thriller against Carlos Alcaraz in the quarter-finals ended at 3:33am local time on Wednesday, leaving few people awake to see the near five-hour marathon reach its finale on one of the sport's biggest stages.

Players have long loved the electricity of playing night matches under the lights in the nation's biggest city.

But the tournament had already set a record with three post-2am finishes over the first six days, as well as having two other matches go past 1am.

The issue ​has gained added resonance amid a broader push by top players for increased prize money and reforms on welfare ‌and working conditions, with late finishes emerging as a flashpoint in the debate over life on the tour.

Like the US Open, the Australian Open has faced criticism for notoriously late ​finishes but the other two Grand Slams have imposed checks, with Wimbledon halting play under an 11pm local curfew and the French Open limiting night sessions to one match.

Yet a solution such as starting evening sessions earlier than 7pm is complicated by the argument that ​tennis-mad New Yorkers need time to get to Flushing Meadows after work and organisers having to manage day-and night-session ⁠crowds.

Tiley said: "I hear from a lot of people that it finishes too late and then I say, okay, and your suggestion is? I don't get anything.

"You can't control the length of the match. What's really interesting is in the last 10 years the amount of tennis from when you hit a point to when a point stops has been about the same.

"But the length of the matches on the men's side has increased by an average of about 25 minutes. That's because we now have the shot clock so everyone is taking their time, and we have the towels here which takes a bit more time and so the whole length of it is a bit longer. Not that much longer, but in fact the average time of the men's matches today is still not in the top four average times in the last 10 years.

"While it feels really late, the reality is you've got to go and look at the data, But that being said, no one wants to finish at 3.30am in the morning, although the rest of the world in the daytime saw a pretty amazing match."

"We really like the two days and two nights. Two full sessions and you get a women's match and a great men's match, and that's what our fans are telling us. They can come out and see three, four, five hours of entertainment and if it goes really long like the other night, that's a great sporting ticket so I will keep it," Tiley added.

"I have higher hopes for myself. So yeah, it's great. The tournament ‌is still going. There's a lot more tennis to be played, a lot more sets to be played, and a lot more physical things to be done. We're going to enjoy this, but we got to keep going."

Tiafoe is enjoying a career resurgence having undertaken a big lifestyle change and fitness regime towards the end of last year.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights of the quarter-final match between Frances Tiafoe and Alex Michelsen

Former world No 1 Lindsay Davenport said: "If you hear their stories about last fall, and what a dark place Frances was in, he was willing to turn over, to try and give it his best shot.

"It's not easy sometimes for players or people to do that, but he has kind of shifted everything in his life to revolve around tennis.

"Now to watch him be able to go out there and compete from two sets down, like the old Frances doesn't necessarily (do), to stick his heels in and be like 'I'm not going anywhere' - I mean, he's fighting."

History awaits...

The winner of Frances Tiafoe vs Ben Shelton will be the first Black American man to reach a US Open Final since Arthur Ashe (1972) and the first Black American man to reach any major final since MaliVai Washington (1996 Wimbledon)



Zverev going about his business

Image: Top seed Alexander Zverev is favourite to win the US Open

While the men's draw has fallen to pieces in the absence of Jannik Sinner and with Novak Djokovic and Alcaraz falling by the wayside, Alexander Zverev has been quietly going about his business.

Luciano Darderi, the 21st seed, is the highest-ranked player Zverev has faced, while he eased past world No 70 Botic van de Zandschulp in straight sets.

The 29-year-old is a big favourite to beat unseeded Russian Karen Khachanov in the opening semi-final on Friday from 8pm on Sky Sports Tennis.

Zverev has beaten Shelton in all five of their career meetings and has lost just one of his 10 matches against Tiafoe.

Having won his first Grand Slam title at this year's French Open and then reached the Wimbledon final, the world No 2 should be feeling at home in the latter stages of major tournaments.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the US Open quarter-final match between Alexander Zverev and Botic van de Zandschulp

But he said: "I think the more often that you get to that stage, the more normal it becomes, which is something that you should never take for granted.

"I know it can change in a heartbeat in tennis. I think confidence is something that is incredibly important, but also can go away quite quickly.

"I found that out after Wimbledon where I didn't play well throughout the two tournaments on the hard courts, and then I found it again here.

"But yeah, of course I'm happy with how things are going, but looking forward, I still hope to play two good matches here."

Sports.title: York Knights finish maiden Super League season with thrashing of Bradford
Sports.content:
Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Highlights from the Super League clash between York Knights and Bradford Bulls. Highlights from the Super League clash between York Knights and Bradford Bulls.

York saw off bottom club Bradford 35-16 in their final match of the regular Super League campaign at the LNER Community Stadium, where Paul Vaughan slotted over a late drop goal on his farewell appearance before retirement.

The Knights - looking to solidify a 10th-place finish in their debut Super League season - had Scott Galeano sent to the sin bin after just 13 minutes following a tip tackle on Phoenix Steinwede, with Bulls then having a try for full-back Caleb Aekins ruled out for a forward offload.

Ryan Sutton made the breakthrough to score the opening try for Bradford after 17 minutes, with Chris Atkin slotting over the extras. The lead, though, was short-lived as Galeano marked his return to the action by showing quick feet to then dive over.

Ben Jones-Bishop, who was given a guard of honour ahead of making his 400th career appearance, added another try for the home side, with Cody Hunter converting for a 12-6 lead.

Bradford rallied again as Riley Dean latched on to a spilled kick to touchdown, but York responded again just before half-time as Toa Mata'afa burst down the middle to send the Knights into the break 18-12 ahead.

Bulls prop Ebon Scurr saw his try early in the second half ruled out for an obstruction, before York got themselves over the line again on 51 minutes when Jesse Dee touched down a deft low kick from Paul McShane.

York were in again when Bradford spilled another high ball and Xavier Va'a slid over before David Nofoaluma also capitalised on poor handling to dot down in the 67th minute.

Jayden Okunbor went over to give Bradford a late consolation try with five minutes left before Australian prop Vaughan, 35, slotted over a drop goal - sparking wild celebrations from his York team-mates.

Sports.title: Man Utd put four past Sabah on Champions League return
Sports.content:
Manchester United made a winning return to the Champions League as they beat Sabah FC in style with a 4-0 victory at Old Trafford.

The Azerbaijani side started brightly but Matheus Cunha converted Patrick Dorgu's 27th-minute cross and, although Joy-Lance Mickels should have levelled, two goals late in the first half from Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko put United in total control.

Michael Carrick made changes in the second half with the points secure but there was still time for Lisandro Martinez to smash home from close range after some flashy play from Joshua Zirkzee, who produced an eye-catching cameo. Signs of that United swagger.

With goal difference a potentially significant factor in the league phase of this Champions League format, this was a fine night's work on their return. It is Atletico Madrid away next in Europe but there are bigger matters to attend to before that.

Analysis: Carrick has options

It is over 1000 days since United competed in a Champions League game but this, their 300th in Europe's premier club competition, was not too taxing for Carrick's men. It will be tougher against rivals Manchester City on Sunday - but so will his team selection.

Some of the calls are obvious. Fernandes starred again and the sight of him combining with the equally intelligent Youri Tielemans for United's second was encouraging. The Belgian produced perhaps his best 45 minutes at Old Trafford. But others pressed their case too.

Image: Youri Tielemans celebrates with Bruno Fernandes during the win over Sabah

Sesko scored after coming off the bench against Everton and looked sharp here in his first start of the season. With Marcus Rashford also available, and Cunha getting a confidence-boosting goal, there are some interesting decisions ahead for the United boss.

Dorgu enjoyed himself at left-back with Luke Shaw missing from the squad but he was able to play as a de facto winger given United's superiority. It will be more challenging against City's attack but Carrick and his players go into that with confidence restored.

The key moments from Old Trafford

27 - GOAL! Cunha converts Dorgu's cross at the near post

36 - SITTER! Mickels nods wide from inside the six-yard box

42 - GOAL! Fernandes makes it two from Tielemans' pass

45 - GOAL! Mbeumo puts Sesko in to round the goalkeeper

68 - GOAL! Zirkzee's backheel finds Martinez who smashes it in

Carrick: Really encouraging

Man Utd boss Michael Carrick speaking in the press conference:

"I think it was kind of what we set out to achieve, good performance, individually and collectively throughout the game, the boys that started, the boys that came on pitch, clean sheet, goals, exciting football. A good night all round.

"Results-wise, it has not been the start that what we wanted. We wanted more points in the league. But performance-wise, it has been a lot of things we are looking for.

"Collectively, as a team, we have done a lot of the right things and that is why were are excited about what the season will bring. It is really encouraging for me."

On the performance of Benjamin Sesko…

"He definitely offers a different kind of threat, that is the beauty of it really, we know what Ben gives us and there are not many who can give us what he gives us. Speed, physicality, ability to play on the last line and run in behind. Great to have him back."

Dambrauskas: Almost impossible to stop

Sabah head coach Valdas Dambrauskas speaking in the press conference:

"I didn't feel like we were shaking or scared, we tried to play, for the whole 90 minutes we did that. We were escaping from time to time from United pressure.

"We will all go home thinking we could have done better, especially the result. The result could have been a little bit smaller.

"We did not have enough courage probably from the back line to get up. Our centre-backs stayed too deep, not afraid but maybe from inexperience we were over-evaluating the opponent.

"Because when you don't squeeze that space and you allow those players to turn and run it is almost impossible to stop them."

What is next for Man Utd...

Sports.title: McIlroy four off Irish Open lead in tough conditions with Lowry near top
Sports.content:
Rory McIlroy battled on against testing blustery conditions at the Amgen Irish Open to sit four shots off the clubhouse lead following a one-under par opening round, with Ireland's Shane Lowry two off the top.

Gusts up to 35mph saw balls oscillating on greens with Frenchman Frederic Lacroix seeing his blown off the putting surface at the 13th, but he had fortunately already marked so was able to replace it.

All of which made for slow going at Trump International Golf Links and Hotel in Doonbeg during Thursday's first round.

As the day wore on, a course-record 65 from Chilean Joaquin Niemann looked increasingly good.

Having reached the turn at two under, Niemann had four successive birdies from the 14th to put him in contention for a $30,000 (£22,000) bonus for the lowest round of the week.

Austrian Maximilian Steinlechner and Renato Paratore appeared set to make a challenge for the top of the leaderboard at three under through 12 and 11 respectively, but could be thwarted by the fading light.

Home favourite Lowry, who won the event as a 22-year-old amateur in Baltray, kept himself in the mix, also in the clubhouse at three under.

Image: Ireland's Lowry sits two shots off the lead following the opening round

Long waits on many tee boxes had been commonplace but McIlroy, who had won the event at the K Club last year, started with two birdies in his first four holes before getting to the turn in a two-under 34 - in three and a half hours.

After missing a four-foot birdie chance at the first he holed a 14-footer at the second, splashed out of a bunker to three feet at the par-five fourth for his second birdie, but missed from 10 feet at the seventh for a third.

McIlroy found the fairway bunker on the 13th, and a missed 10-foot putt saw him take a double-bogey hit before a fine approach to the 15th helped quickly pull a stroke back.

The world No 2, though, could not make the most of what proved limited opportunities over the closing run, narrowly missing a lengthy birdie attempt on the 18th, and will return on Friday morning hoping to improve along with the weather forecast.

McIlroy: A tough day to play in - I hung in there

"There was a couple of things that were tough today. Obviously the wind and the strength of the wind was one thing, and then the pace of play," McIlroy said.

"This course isn't conducive to sort of letting you get in a flow. Especially the first two days with so many people in the field, there is a lot of stopping and starting.

"It's hard when you are playing a round of golf and it takes six hours, it's hard to get into the rhythm of things, but felt like I did a good job.

Sports.title: Sesko soars as Manchester United surge past Sabah on Champions League return
Sports.content:
It was a night for romance given the astonishing story that Sabah brought with them to Old Trafford for their Champions League debut. This is a club that did not even exist a decade ago and nobody saw their bolt to the title in Azerbaijan coming last season; in 2024-25, they had finished 41 points off the top. The job that their manager, Valdas Dambrauskas, has done since taking over in the summer of last year is extraordinary.

It was also a night for cold, hard reality. Manchester United were back in Europe’s elite competition after a two-year hiatus and in need of something to soothe them after the trauma of their last-gasp coughing up of two points in last Sunday’s Premier League draw at Everton. And before the extremely serious business of the derby here against Manchester City on Sunday. They got it on the back of a first-half performance that burned slowly before catching fire.

Sabah were game. United were clinical. It was Matheus Cunha who broke the deadlock midway through the first half and the defining moments came at the end of the period when Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko sent United into half-time with a three-goal cushion. Lisandro Martínez added the fourth late on. It was a case of job done for Michael Carrick, no wobbles. Now for City.

United had wanted to put their best foot forward when they heard the Champions League aria after the chaos and embarrassment of their previous involvement in the competition. Erik ten Hag was the manager in 2023-24 and his team finished bottom of their group with four points, starting and ending with losses to Bayern Munich. It was what happened in between times against Galatasaray and Copenhagen that still causes a few shudders. It was a period when United panicked uncontrollably when they had a lead. When the defensive gifts from them came in crazy clusters.

Carrick took no chances with his starting XI. There was minimal rotation in the midfield and front line, save for a first start of the season for Sesko in the No 9 position. It was easy to think that the manager wanted to groove Youri Tielemans and Kobbie Mainoo in central midfield before the City game.

United looked to Fernandes to get them going. As always. There were intelligent runs from him; incision about his passes, that wonderful disguise on some of them. The breakthrough goal stemmed from him chasing a high ball over the top that looked like a lost cause only for him to keep it in play. It was what happened next that quickened United pulses. When Sabah gave the ball away cheaply to Bryan Mbeumo, United moved quickly over to the left. Patrick Dorgu crossed and Cunha’s finish was clean.

Quick Guide Gabriel, 15, stars with hat-trick for United in Youth League debut Show Manchester United's JJ Gabriel (pictured) marked his Uefa Youth League debut with a hat-trick against Sabah aged just 15. The attacker is tipped as a future star and made his first appearance for the first team off the bench in last month’s friendly against Atlético Madrid. Gabriel has yet to make Michael Carrick’s squad for a competitive match but the teenager, who turns 16 next month, continues to knock on the door. He sparkled for the Under-19s in Thursday’s 5-0 win against Sabah in the Youth League in front of director of football Jason Wilcox, director of recruitment Christopher Vivell and first-team coach Travis Binnion. Amir Ibragimov and Jacob Watson scored early goals in Leigh, where Gabriel added another in a dominant first half. Gabriel scored two more late in the second half to claim the match ball against the Azerbaijani visitors, who did not manage a shot on a day that United mustered 44 attempts. PA Photograph: Zohaib Alam/Manchester United Was this helpful? Thank you for your feedback.

Sabah lined up in a 4-3-3 formation; no bus parking. They wanted to ask questions of a United defence that had a makeshift feel about it. There was assurance on the ball from them, the desire to carry it forward. And a huge chance in the 35th minute when Kaheem Parris crossed to the back post. Joy-Lance Mickels was clear of Noussair Mazraoui only to put the header wide. The angle was not favourable. It did not entirely excuse him.

View image in fullscreen Matheus Cunha opens the scoring with a smart finish in the first half. Photograph: Stu Forster/Getty Images

Sabah were harshly treated by the half-time scoreline, even though United played on the front foot and created openings. It was the one-two punch in the closing stages of the first period that changed everything. Fernandes – who else? – made a sidefoot finish look easy after Tielemans had burst on a Cunha pass inside, spun and teed him up. The third followed a first time pass by Fernandes into Mbeumo, who got Sesko clean though. The Sabah backline was high. Sesko went around the goalkeeper to score. He never looked like missing.

There was a lovely scene 90 ­minutes before kick-off when some of the Sabah players wandered around the pitch, the stadium virtually empty, phones out to capture the quiet before the storm, the sheer scale of Old Trafford. They wore wide smiles. They were determined not to be overawed when it got started. The performance of the strolling central midfielder, Ivan Lepinjica, was certainly impressive. They were just too loose at the back.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

United played some slick stuff at times, Mainoo and ­Fernandes ever involved. When Carrick’s ­pass-and-move game clicks, it is easy to feel the ­possibility. ­Imposing it against the higher-­profile teams is the name of the game. ­Starting against City.

Mason Mount was introduced at half-time for his first football of the season – “It was great to get Mason back on the pitch,” Carrick later said – with Tielemans coming off, his work done. The Belgian could be pleased with his impact. Carrick was always going to withdraw other likely starters against City, such as Mainoo. Sesko came off with him on 64 minutes and was warmly applauded. After his goal at Everton on Sunday, has he done enough to make the XI for the derby?

Carrick added: “We always push for more. Results-wise it hasn’t been the start we wanted, but performance-wise there are a lot of things we were looking for. The clean sheet was important tonight. Collectively as a team we have done a lot of good things and that is why we are excited what this season can bring.”

His side controlled the second half. The jeopardy was long gone. The fourth goal summed up Sabah’s travails in their defensive third. It was a scooped free-kick by Fernandes for Joshua Zirkzee, on as a substitute, and when his backheel hit Aden ­McCarthy, the Sabah goalkeeper, Stas Pokatilov, lost his bearings, the ball caught under his feet. It was a tap-in for Martínez. The substitute, Orphé Mbina, headed high for Sabah at the very end. There was to be no fairytale goal.

Sports.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
Sports.content:
1 Ton up for hard-working McBurnie

With 10 top-flight goal contributions between them across three games already this season, the Chelsea trio of Morgan Rogers, João Pedro and Cole Palmer are the early pace-setters for the Premier League’s most prolific, fluid and high octane attacking unit. But on the occasion of his 100th Premier League appearance, a scruffier and more ungainly unit will be hoping to steal their thunder, as high-flying Hull try to register a top-flight win against Chelsea for the very first time. Yet to score this season but with a couple of near-misses to his name, what Oli McBurnie has thus far lacked in goal contributions he has more than made up for with selfless graft and off-the-ball grunt work, making a total mockery of Steve Clarke’s decision not to include him in Scotland’s World Cup squad. The Hull striker ought to prove a real handful for a decidedly porous home defence, and a goal would be a fitting way to mark a century of Premier League appearances. Chelsea have not won any of their past four league matches against promoted opposition and given Hull’s blistering start to the season, victory on Saturday seems anything but a foregone conclusion. Barry Glendenning

Chelsea v Hull, Saturday 3pm (all times BST)

2 Arbeloa must trust process as Iraola once did

This might be an opportune moment for Álvaro Arbeloa to meet Andoni Iraola, though perhaps not his Liverpool team. With three defeats from his first three Premier League games as Fulham head coach, and seven goals conceded, questions are already being asked over the former Liverpool defender’s ambitious approach. Just as they were when Iraola failed to win any of his first nine league games in charge of Bournemouth. Trust yourself and the process, might be the Liverpool head coach’s advice if asked. Fulham have been creative under Arbeloa but are easily exposed defensively. Liverpool, starting to click in attack under their new manager, have the assets to exploit Fulham’s weaknesses and subject Arbeloa to an uncomfortable Anfield return. Iraola’s wide options could be reduced, however, with Bradley Barcola suffering cramp on Wednesday – his first start since France’s World Cup semi-final loss – and Cody Gakpo nursing a minor injury. Andy Hunter

Liverpool v Fulham, Saturday 3pm

3 Doucouré eagerly waiting Palace return

Cheick Doucouré has had a rotten run of luck with injuries. Just when the Mali midfielder looked as if he was ready to make a first Crystal Palace appearance since January 2025 in Tuesday’s Carabao Cup win over Middlesbrough, he was taken ill. Pierre Sage revealed last week that Doucouré looked as if he had “given him one million dollars” when he was informed he would be part of the matchday squad at Fulham, where Palace got off the mark with a 3-2 victory. Sage has confirmed that the 26-year-old, who has been sidelined with two serious knee injuries but was once a transfer target for Liverpool, could be involved against Ipswich at Selhurst Park on Saturday. Whenever he does return it is sure to be a heartwarming moment. Ed Aarons

Crystal Palace v Ipswich, Saturday 3pm

View image in fullscreen Cheick Doucouré returned to the Crystal Palace squad for last weekend’s trip to Fulham. Photograph: James Fearn/Getty Images

4 Cherries must end late lapses

The midfield battle between Brentford and Bournemouth will be crucial on Saturday with Vitaly Janelt and Mamadou Sangaré setting the tempo for Keith Andrews’ physical side. Brentford top the Premier League for aerial duels won (22.3 per 90 mins), interceptions (11.3 per 90), and fouls committed (16.3 per 90). “They defend well as a team, their high pressing is good,” said Bournemouth’s Marco Rose, who is hoping to guide his side to a first Premier League victory of the season. “Their transition, they have fast players. They have quality everywhere on the pitch, and every situation.” Rose’s answer for Brentford’s aggressiveness should be Alex Scott, who leads his team for interceptions and has drawn nine fouls so far this campaign – the fourth-highest tally in the league. Late drama could also be the deciding factor at the Vitality Stadium. Despite leading in all three of their opening league fixtures, Bournemouth have picked up just two points and four of their five goals conceded have arrived from the 84th minute onwards. History favours their opponents too, as the Cherries have failed to win any of their eight top-flight meetings with the Bees. Yara El-Shaboury

Bournemouth v Brentford, Saturday 3pm

5 Jackson ready to fill Watkins’ Villa boots

A summer of change at Aston Villa inevitably prompted plenty of noise but most of their new signings were long-standing targets, none more so than Nicolas Jackson. Unai Emery kickstarted Jackson’s career at Villarreal and after reuniting at Villa, the Senegal striker registered his first goal at Club Brugge on Tuesday after his initial £47.5m move. Jackson has replaced Ollie Watkins, who proved a reliable source of goals across six straight top-flight seasons, and the early evidence has been encouraging. “I had a couple of fights with him when he was at Chelsea so when he first came in I thought: ‘What’s he going to be like?’ but he’s a brilliant guy,” said the Villa captain, John McGinn. “There’s a lot of expectation with the transfer fee but he’s going to be a huge player for us.” Ben Fisher

Aston Villa v Nottingham Forest, Saturday 3pm

6 Signs of early season panic at Spurs

Only the most pessimistic home fans at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium will be gripped by anything resembling the kind of dread, anxiety and outright terror that accompanied Everton’s visit on the final day of last season, but the return of David Moyes’ side so early in the current campaign will still make for nervous viewing. With no goals and just one point on the board after three league games, fan faith in Roberto De Zerbi – and the hundreds of millions of pounds lavished upon new signings – has created a prevailing presumption that Tottenham will soon start firing on at least some, if not all, cylinders. In Everton, Spurs welcome a team whose record in this corner of north London is worse than any other top-flight side. Should they fail to beat a team who have taken just seven points from the past 51 available to them away at Tottenham, the sounds of early but outright mutiny are likely to be audible from the stands. BG

Tottenham v Everton, Saturday 5.30pm

7 Stadium of Light to give Guimarães hot reception

Old acquaintance will be renewed at the Stadium of Light on Saturday evening. While Sunderland’s captain and midfield anchor, Granit Xhaka, needs no introduction to his former north London public, the home centre-half Dan Ballard is a former Arsenal youth captain who joined the Gunners’ academy at the age of eight. Then there is Bruno Guimarães. Newcastle’s former captain can expect a hot reception as his new side aim to extend their season-opening run of five straight wins (including the Community Shield). “Arsenal are flying, they’re one of the best teams in Europe,” says Régis Le Bris, Sunderland’s manager. “It will be challenging but I’m very excited to experience this situation again.” Thanks to goals from Ballard and Brian Brobbey, Le Bris choreographed a 2-2 Premier League draw against Mikel Arteta’s side on Wearside last November. “When you face a strong opponent you can become a bit shy but the most important thing is to be ourselves,” says Le Bris. “Arsenal are so adaptive they will find solutions, so we must be flexible.” Louise Taylor

Sunderland v Arsenal, Saturday 8pm

View image in fullscreen Bruno Guimarães returns to the northeast as Arsenal visit Sunderland on Saturday night. Photograph: David Price/Arsenal FC/Getty Images

8 Coventry adding points to performances?

One of three teams, along with Aston Villa and Tottenham, yet to score a top-flight goal this season, Coventry were extremely unfortunate not to break their duck at Manchester City last weekend. Having narrowly avoided handing Frank Lampard’s side an early opener, it took a string of excellent saves from Gianluigi Donnarumma to ensure City took three points at the death. “They played really well against Manchester City and created a lot of chances,” said Fabian Hürzeler, who takes his Brighton team to the CBS Arena on Sunday afternoon. Having been scathing in his criticism of his own side’s lack of energy and intensity in their woeful first-half performance against Leeds, the German will be aware that a similarly lethargic performance from his team is unlikely to go unpunished. Particularly away from home against a promoted team that may be firing blanks, but visibly grew in confidence with each passing minute of their defeat to one of the league’s best teams. BG

Coventry v Brighton, Sunday 2pm

9 Contrasting Manchester teams face off in derby

Manchester derby No 199 features a fascinating showdown between two young managers operating in the sport’s rarefied air: Michael Carrick, 45, who bids to guide Manchester United to an 82nd victory in the fixture, and Enzo Maresca, 46, who aims for Manchester City’s 63rd. As the great Pep Guardiola’s successor, the visiting Italian can be delighted at his team’s perfect record from their four games under him since the Community Shield. Carrick, though, should be disappointed at the return from an opening three matches as United’s permanent manager: a defeat at Hull and draw at Everton, with the 5-2 home win over Ipswich sandwiched between. United fans will protest beforehand about the club’s approach to eradicating ticket touting, the occasion should be particularly spicy and vibrant. Jamie Jackson

Manchester United v Manchester City, Sunday 4.30pm

View image in fullscreen Manchester United supporters protested ticket touts earlier in the season and will do so again before the Manchester derby. Photograph: Lee Smith/Action Images/Reuters

10 Battle of the goalkeepers at Elland Road

Two teams unbeaten in the Premier League this season, two German managers in the dugouts and a Monday night goalkeeping beauty contest at Elland Road. While Daniel Farke welcomes his compatriot, Matthias Jaissle, to West Yorkshire for the first time, James Trafford – the £40m England keeper Newcastle tried to sign on three separate occasions – will be in goal for Leeds. The visitors eventually turned their attentions to the £26m Czechia goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek, who arrived on Tyneside from Braga in July. So far at least, Jaissle is delighted by the 24-year-old’s performances. “Lukas is an amazing signing who has been amazing,” said Eddie Howe’s successor. “Coming to the Premier League and dealing with the pressure is not easy and, as a keeper, that pressure is something else. I like Lukas a lot. He’s so calm but so mature as well. There’s not even a hint of nervousness. He gives the whole team confidence. That helps a lot.” LT

Sports.title: Clearlake Capital close on buying out Chelsea co-owners Todd Boehly and Mark Walter
Sports.content:
Chelsea’s majority owners, Clearlake Capital, are closing in on an agreement to buy out co-owners Todd Boehly and Mark Walter in a deal that would see the pair make a profit on their investment and value the club at around £5bn.

On-off discussions between the two ownership groups over a potential sale have been taking place for the last two years, but intensified last month as a result of Mark Walter seeking to raise funds to pay off insurers following a US federal investigation over alleged tax fraud.

Walter, Boehly and Swiss billionaire Hansjörg Wyss all own 12.8% of Chelsea following their joint £2.5bn purchase of the club with Clearlake from Roman Abramovich four years ago, in a deal in which the new owners commit to spending a further £1.75bn on the club.

Under the terms of their ownership agreement, none of Chelsea’s shareholders can sell to a third party without the consent of their partners giving Clearlake, whose investment is managed by Behdad Eghbali and José E Feliciano, an exclusive option to purchase Boehly and Walter’s stakes.

In a statement issued to Bloomberg a spokesperson for Walter confirmed that he is seeking a sale with an agreement close. Boehly is also expected to sell as he is a long-time investment partner of Walters. Wyss’s position is unconfirmed.

“This potential transaction values Mark Walter’s stake in Chelsea Football Club at a premium to his initial investment and is another successful sports investment for him,” a spokesperson for Walter said.

“After this exit, Mr Walter intends to make future sports-related investments. “Walter did not initiate the proposed transaction to sell his interest, which has been in the works for quite some time.”

As 61.5% shareholders, Clearlake already had day-to-day operational control at Chelsea managed by Eghbali, and were due to make their own appointment as chairman to replace Boehly next year, but taking complete control will ease internal tensions at the club and should smooth decision making.

The most immediate impact of the impending ownership change is likely to be felt in Chelsea’s plans for a new stadium, as Eghbali has clashed with Boehly over whether the club should seek to redevelop Stamford Bridge or seek an alternative site elsewhere.

Walter is being investigated by the US Department of Justice over $21bn in loans which it has been alleged were not disclosed to state insurance regulators, and led to the sudden sale of assets to pay down some of the loans.

The American insurance and sports investor last month sold his 85% stake in the Los Angeles Lakers to Josh ⁠Kushner and Bob Iger in a deal that valued the NBA franchise at around £9bn.

Walter’s holding company, TWG Global, subsequently issued a statement saying that the company “is not looking to sell its sports assets at ‘fire sale’ prices”.

Representatives for Boehly and Clearlake declined to comment.

Sports.title: Champions League: Bayern break down Bodø/Glimt, Como put four past Leipzig
Sports.content:
Bayern Munich opened their Champions League campaign with a 5-0 thrashing of Norway’s Bodo/Glimt.

The six-times winners were frustrated before half-time by Bodo/Glimt but cruised once Jamal Musiala smashed in the opener two minutes into the second period and the floodgates opened.

Harry Kane headed the second on the hour – his 34th goal in 39 Champions League appearances for Bayern – and Alphonso Davies made it 3-0 with a powerful half-volley. With Vincent Kompany’s side in full flow, Michael ‌Olise completed the scoring with a superb late brace.

Cesc Fàbregas’s Como impressed on their debut in Europe’s premier club competition, crushing RB Lepzig 4-1.

Goals from Croatia midfielder Martin Baturina, Greece forward Tasos Douvikas and Senegal’s Assane Diao put Como in control. Serbia midfielder Andrija Maksimović pulled a goal back for Leipzig, before Maximo Perrone sealed a 4-1 victory late on in a dream night in northern Italy.

View image in fullscreen Como manager Cesc Fàbregas gives a post-game, on-pitch team talk to his players after opening the Italian side’s Champions League campaign with a win. Photograph: Alex Pantling/UEFA/Getty Images

Ten-man Slavia Prague suffered ​heartbreak at home to Lens ‌as they conceded twice in ​stoppage time to lose 3-2.

Mikulas ​Konecny was sent off for the hosts just after half-time after a tackle was reviewed by VAR, but minutes later Danijel Sturm put the hosts ahead. Abdallah Sima broke Slavia’s resistance with an equaliser only for Sturm to send the home crowd into raptures with his second in the 88th minute.

Florian Thauvin struck in the 91st minute and there was still time for Lens to snatch victory with a pinpoint strike by Ruben Aguilar.
