PSV came from a goal down to draw 1-1 at home to Shakhtar Donetsk and end a woeful record in their opening matches of Champions League campaigns. The Dutch club had lost their opening fixtures in their last five Champions League appearances and trailed at half-time before Sergiño Dest ensured a point.

Right near the end of a cagey first half, Shakhtar stunned the hosts when Gleiker Mendoza cut in from wide and ‌sent a stunning low ‌shot beyond the dive of Matej Kovar. PSV responded immediately after the break as the ‌ball was fed across the area to Dest who calmly found the bottom corner with an inch-perfect shot.

Roma drew 1-1 with Fenerbahce in Istanbul, with Bryan Cristante’s opener for the visitors cancelled out by Archie Brown’s goal three minutes into the second half. Confusion reigned after the match as the Fenerbahce head coach, Ismail Kartal, announced his resignation – only for the club president to insist he will stay.

Sports.title: French FA accuses Infantino of ‘seriously damaging’ football as it withdraws support
Sports.content:
The French Football Federation’s president, Philippe Diallo, said Gianni Infantino had “seriously damaged the image and the unity of football” as he announced the end of France’s support for the Fifa president’s re-election.

The FFF’s executive committee unanimously voted on Thursday to withdraw its backing, which had been formalised at the end of June. Diallo referred to “events during the World Cup” which had “flagrantly gone against the way we believe our sport should be run” and to Infantino’s World Cup sell-off plan, which was revealed in July and scrapped after a widespread backlash.

During the World Cup the suspension of the US forward Folarin Balogun was overturned by Fifa after lobbying from Donald Trump. The US president said he called Infantino to recommend that Balogun be allowed to play. Fifa has said the decision taken by its disciplinary committee was “a balanced measure” and “based on an explicit provision of the applicable regulations”.

Diallo outlined the reasons for the loss in confidence: “From July onwards, the conditions which led to us to support his candidacy had been disrupted. Does the withdrawal of the [sell-off] project solve the issue? I don’t think so. His initiatives during and after the World Cup have seriously damaged the image and the unity of football. As a result, we believe that trust has been broken.”

Diallo said of the initial decision to support Infantino: “It would be wrong to say that certain developments in football were not made under his mandate.” But he added: “When you are making changes to the game itself, in a unilateral and opaque fashion to sell our shared asset, that changes our appreciation.

“France is one of the founding members of Fifa, and as such we have a historical legitimacy to intervene when we feel that Fifa and its president are deviating from our vision of how world football should be run. We also have sporting legitimacy, as one of the top three teams in the world rankings over the last 10 years. We wanted to make it clear that we refuse to go in a direction which does not correspond to the general interest of our sport.”

When reports of the sell-off project came to light, the FFF expressed “doubts and deep concerns”. Uefa threatened a boycott of Fifa competitions and several European countries, including Wales and England, withdrew their support for Infantino but the FFF had not until Thursday publicly disavowed him.

Diallo indicated France would play an active part in Uefa’s search for an alternative candidate for the Fifa presidency before the 18 November deadline. The election will take place in March during Fifa’s next congress.

Before then, Diallo said, the FFF would reach out to figures it considers experts in “transparency and good governance” in football and beyond as part of France’s “contribution to the debate”, as it pushes for “far-reaching reform” of Fifa.

He cited Kevin Lamour, the former Fifa chief operating officer who was dismissed after criticising the sell-off plan, as one of the people the FFF would look to consult.

Fifa was approached for comment.

Sports.title: Fenerbahce coach resigns after draw with Roma – but president insists he will stay
Sports.content:
The Fenerbahce head coach, Ismail Kartal, announced his resignation on Thursday after ⁠his team drew 1-1 at home to Roma in the Champions League – but minutes ⁠later, the club ⁠president ​said Kartal would stay in the job.

Kartal shocked the post-match press conference by claiming he was ⁠leaving Fenerbahce “never to return”. The 65-year-old added that he was taking the drastic decision “to clear the way for the club” – but the Fenerbahce president, Aziz Yildrim, quickly moved to play down his manager’s remarks.

Minutes after ⁠the press conference, Yildirim told reporters that ​Kartal “continues in his role” with the Turkish side. “Some ‌fans threw a bottle ‌at the coach’s head this evening during the game. He ‌is upset about it,” the club president added.

“I just spoke to Ismail Kartal. He mentioned the bottle incident and he also complained about being under pressure,” he said. Asked whether the manager had told him he would stay, Yildirim said: “There’s no need for him ‌to say that he’d continue. I am his senior, I told him to continue and that’s ​it. We are a family.”

Kartal, who spent a decade at Fenerbahce as a player, coached the club in 2014-15, then on an interim basis in 2021-22 before returning for a full ⁠campaign in 2023-24. He was the assistant manager at Fenerbahce the ​past two ​times the club won ​the Turkish title, and returned for a fourth ​managerial spell in ‌June.

View image in fullscreen Archie Brown celebrates his equaliser for Fenerbahce. The English full-back was left dumbfounded when learning of his coach’s resignation after the final whistle. Photograph: Anadolu/Getty Images

Fenerbahce have ​finished second ​in the Turkish Super Lig in each of the past five seasons, and reached the Champions League’s league phase this season for the first time in 18 years. The team sit ninth in the Turkish top-flight, having lost twice in their opening four games, including Saturday’s 2-1 home defeat to Besiktas.

Roma took the lead in the 39th minute when Donyell Malen rolled a pass to ​Bryan Cristante, who beat Fenerbahce keeper Ederson with a bouncing finish. The hosts levelled before half-time when Mason Greenwood slipped a ​pass through to Archie ​Brown, who clipped a finish over ​Mile Svilar.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Roma were awarded a penalty in the 68th minute when ​Kerem Akturkoglu was ‌penalised for a ​foul on Paulo ​Dybala, but a VAR check ruled that the challenge had taken place outside the area. Fenerbahce came closest to grabbing a winner late on when Nathan Aké headed against the Roma crossbar.

Fenerbahce will travel to Aston Villa and host Liverpool in two of their remaining league phase games – whether Kartal will be in charge or not remains to be seen.

Sports.title: Mauricio Pochettino: ‘I am always open to help Tottenham. In whatever division’
Sports.content:
If things had worked out differently, Mauricio Pochettino would have gone back to his beloved Tottenham over the summer. They had put in the call and it stirred him. Nothing was going to put him off – not even the possibility of the club being in the Championship.

Seriously, Mauricio? After a World Cup campaign with the United States and top jobs with Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain before that, he would have been willing to start a new chapter in the second tier of English football? “Yes, of course,” Pochettino says. “Tottenham … it’s the only club that always I am open to help. In whatever division.”

Football is about timing and Pochettino was left to reflect on how his stars did not align. It has been a theme of his managerial career, along with the desire to keep an eye out for greener pastures. And not be shy about doing so.

Spurs’ idea after sacking Thomas Frank in February was to get to the end of the season under the interim Igor Tudor, when they could assess a potentially deeper pool of candidates. They knew that if Pochettino was to be their man, they would have to wait for him because he was contracted to the US until after the World Cup. There was no way he could walk out on that challenge. Nor would he have wanted to.

Then the picture changed. When Tudor bombed, leaving Spurs one point above the relegation zone with seven games to play, they pivoted to Roberto De Zerbi, who said no to them after they dismissed Frank. De Zerbi had just left Marseille and needed a break. Now Spurs made him a long-term offer he could not refuse. And so Pochettino felt the door close to the club where he managed for five-and-a-half years from 2014; where he established such a strong connection.

“The problem was that the timings were never the best,” he says. “When I was free, I never received a contact and then when I was working, I received a contact but I cannot make the decision to come back. It was a little bit unlucky. Maybe one day the stars will align and it can happen. If I was free, of course, I come. But I wasn’t free. I was preparing the World Cup.”

View image in fullscreen Mauricio Pochettino, celebrating after the dramatic semi-final win against Ajax, led Tottenham to the Champions League final in 2019. Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/Reuters

Was the door to Spurs ever truly open for Pochettino? The club have insisted that De Zerbi was their No 1 target for the summer before they were forced to move ahead of time. Perhaps we will never know. But one thing is clear: these kind of teasers and Pochettino’s openness about them are a part of his story. They add to his swaggering appeal. In a game where micromanaged content is the norm, where managers are tied in knots by the party line, there is something exhilarating about hearing Pochettino hold court.

The 54-year-old has always had his suitors, ever since he first began to establish his reputation as a forward-thinking coach and charismatic man-manager at Espanyol, where he took charge in 2009. He has always liked to keep them close and he always will do. Should US Soccer be worried? Pochettino has just signed a new four-year contract to take him up to the 2030 World Cup. That is probably an unhealthy way of thinking. Better for the federation to focus on how it has one of the game’s elite managers and accept that they will have options.

View image in fullscreen Mauricio Pochettino has signed a new deal with the United States that will take him through to the 2030 World Cup. Photograph: Todd Kirkland/FIFA/Getty Images

Pochettino has had his share of sliding-doors moments. He was linked to the Real Madrid job in November 2017 as Zinedine Zidane was tipped for the sack only for the Frenchman to hang on and end up winning the Champions League that season. Two days before the final against Liverpool, Pochettino signed a new long-term contract at Spurs. Five days after it, Zidane announced his shock resignation. It was not the first or, indeed, the last time that Pochettino was linked to Madrid.

There have been links with Manchester United. The club considered him when they sacked Louis van Gaal in 2016, when they dismissed José Mourinho in 2018 and turned to Ole Gunnar Solskjær, initially on an interim basis (Solskjær would make the job his own), and before they hired Erik ten Hag in 2022.

Then there was England. Pochettino was in the conversation as the Football Association looked for a successor to Sir Gareth Southgate after Euro 2024. The way Pochettino tells it, he committed to the US in August of that year and it was before the FA started its search in earnest. It would end with it choosing Thomas Tuchel.

Would Pochettino consider the England job one day? He is aware that his Argentinian nationality would present an issue – because of the Falklands conflict and the history between the countries on the football pitch. It was fractious when they clashed in the World Cup semi-final in July, Argentina winning 2-1. But Pochettino does not see it as a deal-breaker.

“Maybe, yes,” he says of coaching England. “If you consider in a few years’ time, yes … if I got an approach. One thing I don’t want because the USA guys will kill me is if you say the headline is: ‘Mauricio will consider English job.’ It is like I am considering it now. No. Not now. If I am free [in the future].

View image in fullscreen Mauricio Pochettino, still adored by Tottenham fans, says the north London team is ‘still my club’. Photograph: Tony O’Brien/Action Images/Reuters

“My respect is that it’s football. I am the first to feel for my people in Argentina but at the end of the day it’s just football. The World Cup semi-final was just one game of football, although people wanted to convert it to other subjects. It is true that it can be controversial because an Argentinian guy is thinking to maybe one day defend the flag of England and we were involved in a war …”

Pochettino still has his family home in north London. He has a love affair with the city and England. “We are very similar, Argentinian and English people, in the way we feel the passion of football,” he says. “I love the countryside here, too. I think you respect all the things that I also grew up with in my country.

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Twice weekly Sign up to Soccer Desk Jonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer. Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

“In Argentina, I lived in a town in Murphy with a lot of Irish and British people around. And all the clubs … Racing Club, River Plate, Newell’s Old Boys. They are English language names, no? Now I am here doing my passion that is football and I cannot work here [for England]? Why? It is crazy. I really believe in the diplomatic things, going to talk and for sure to find the best way.”

Pochettino extended his contract with the US for many reasons, among them the faith the federation had shown in him. They offered him the four-year deal before the World Cup kicked off, which he appreciated greatly. He signed it in August. The challenge excites him – to change the perception of the game in the country, to build something. He has made a good start.

The World Cup ended badly with the 4-1 defeat by Belgium in the last 16. The game was overshadowed by the Folarin Balogun controversy; how the US federation was able to overturn the striker’s suspension amid trademark grandstanding from Donald Trump. It ought to have been a blessing. It ended up as a curse, affecting Balogun and the team; giving Belgium even more of a cause. But before that, everything had gone extremely well.

View image in fullscreen Mauricio Pochettino managed USA to the last-16 of this summer’s World Cup. Photograph: Alex Livesey/FIFA/Getty Images

The free-flowing 4-1 victory against Paraguay in the opening game sparked a feelgood factor. Then came the comfortable win over Australia to secure qualification from the group with a game to spare. Bosnia and Herzegovina were swatted aside in the last 32. “We created something,” Pochettino says. “The fans were amazing. We never expected the fans in this way. The players changed completely the mindset.”

Pochettino’s situation, though, does feel different with the longer contract – certainly to him. “Now it is a different thing,” he says. “When we gave our word to the federation [in August 2024], it was about starting and finishing after the World Cup. For us, it was the moment to say: ‘If some club comes, it’s impossible.’ Always you can break a contract, say you stop and that’s it … you agree something. But in the moment it wasn’t right for us to create all these situations and expectations.

“Now it’s a four-year contract, it’s different. We can next season lose the Copa América or the Gold Cup, they’re not happy with us and they can sack us. Or we can say: ‘OK. It’s not in the way that we think.’ Four years is different. Maybe now if someone calls in the future, it’s a different, different type [of thing]. We are excited, we are thinking to spend four years to the next World Cup. But now it’s a long period.”

The conversation turns back to Spurs. As it often does with Pochettino. He says his former striker Harry Kane, who is at Bayern Munich, would be a deserving winner of this year’s Ballon d’Or. He insists he was pleased to see De Zerbi get more than £300m to spend on players over the summer; a figure he could only have dreamed about. “I am happy because I feel Tottenham … it’s still my club,” Pochettino says. And there is another window into his soul when he reflects on how Spurs got rid of the longstanding chair, Daniel Levy, last September – the man who dismissed him.

“I think he feels like I did when I was sacked,” Pochettino says. “I keep in touch with him and I never made the situation personal because you can sack a coach. The way I felt in that moment … you receive the letter, you pick up your things and you can never come back to say goodbye to the people, maybe 200, 300 people, that were your family. You cannot send a text, you cannot do nothing.

“That was really, really tough for me and I was talking with him [Levy] about that. Of course, I am not happy that now he feels the same because I am not a person who has bad feelings. But yes, it’s difficult for him and his family and I am so sorry for him.”

Pochettino is ready for the next phase of his US adventure. As ever, his mind and heart race with possibility.

Sports.title: Declan Rice shrugs off Arsenal concerns and says 60 games a season is sustainable
Sports.content:
Declan Rice has insisted his body can sustain more than 60 appearances again this season, despite Arsenal’s concerns after he played through pain at the World Cup.

Rice racked up 69 appearances last season for Arsenal and England but revealed during the World Cup he had been managing neural back and hamstring pain, for which he is understood to have received a pain-killing injection, after a hamstring injury in December. It is understood Arsenal are monitoring the 27-year-old’s workload closely after he had only three weeks off before returning to training a week before the Community Shield last month.

Rice came off the bench to replace Bruno Guimarães in the victory over Manchester City in Cardiff and has since started all Arsenal’s matches, with Guimarães’ return from an injury being managed. A major reason why Arsenal bought the Brazil midfielder for £75m from Newcastle was to take some strain off from Rice, although it was noticeable that Rice played all of Wednesday’s Champions League victory at Napoli, with Mikel Merino coming off for Guimarães.

“I think for the last six seasons, even since my West Ham days when they were in Europe, I’ve played 60-plus every season,” Rice said. “So I think it is sustainable because I’ve shown that I can do it.

“It’s just about maintaining it, maintaining the level and the consistency of the performances. For me, that’s the main thing, showing up every week, giving a good account of myself and helping the team win. I’ve been lucky enough to be able to do that. So I’m really hungry to be able to do that again this season.”

It is understood Arsenal offered Rice more time off after the World Cup exploits but that he was keen to return for the start of the season. He is expected to be part of Thomas Tuchel’s squad for Nations League fixtures against Spain, Czechia and Croatia when it is announced next Friday, although whether he features in all four matches remains to be seen, with Arsenal likely to request that he and Bukayo Saka are given another opportunity to rest. Rice said he had found things “tough” during the World Cup but is adamant he is feeling “refreshed”.

“I feel really good at the minute, in really good form, so we’ll make it continue,” he said. “I think everyone knew I had an issue with a neural hamstring. But also on the top of the Premier League season, which was so demanding, the Champions League, to then play a World Cup in that heat really does take its toll. I’m a player that goes on the pitch, wants to be fresh and give 100% every time I put on an England shirt. Yes, there were stages where I felt really, really good and stages where I didn’t feel so good. There were a few things that frustrated me, just with myself, just not feeling 100%. It’s one of those things I just had to manage.”

skip past newsletter promotion Free newsletter | Every weekday Sign up to Football Daily Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football Enter your email Sign up after newsletter promotion

Rice is one of three England players nominated for the Ballon d’Or this week, with Jude Bellingham and Harry Kane. The ceremony, traditionally in Paris, will take place in London on 26 October as a tribute to Sir Stanley Matthews, who won the inaugural award in 1956, and Rice has backed Kane to become the first English winner since Michael Owen in 2001. “I would Iove to see Harry win it,” he said. “So I’m wishing him all the best in that.”

Sports.title: Stunned Fenerbahce player has to double take during interview after learning manager resigned
Sports.content:
Stunned Fenerbahce player has to double take during interview after learning manager resigned

Fenerbahce defender Archie Brown couldn't believe what he heard after being told his manager had instantly quit post-match.

Ismail Kartal announced that he would be resigning from his post straight after a draw with Roma in the Champions League.



2 Brown was completely baffled by the news that his manager had quit

Speaking in his post-match press conference, Kartal shockingly confirmed that he would be stepping down.

It caught everyone off guard - even his own players - with Brown being left completely baffled during his own interview.

As he stood in front of journalist, he was told by a translator from the Fenerbahce staff that Kartal had left.



And as soon as he heard, Brown quickly swung his head around with a confused expression, asking: "What do you mean he resigned?"

The Englishman then looked around as he took the news in, with it being confirmed that Kartal announced he had quit during his press conference.



Brown then asked again: "[Quit] as what? As coach?

"What do you mean by resigned... he's not coach anymore? He said this just now? I didn't know about this."

Kartal's resignation marked a disappointing end to a productive night for Brown, who had scored in Fenerbahce's draw.



In fact, the left-back won the Player of the Match award following the 1-1- draw with Serie A side Roma in Istanbul.

His strike just after half time helped his side claim a point in their league phase opener.

2 Kartal quit his job when speaking to the media post-match on Thursday Credit: Getty

Why did Ismail Kartal resign?

Fenerbahce manager Kartal left his job minutes after the full-time whistle and vowed never to return to the club.



This was his fourth stint in charge of the Turkish giants.

“I am resigning from my position while there is still time," he said. "I am resigning with the understanding that I will never return.

“I have been here for three months. From the beginning of the season until today, the training sessions and camps I conducted with my players… our president and managers tried to help us in every way. Those were wonderful days.

"As of this evening, I congratulate my players and I am resigning from my position.

“Therefore, I would like to thank all my fans, media members, staff, and fellow players who have supported me until today.



“I made this decision to pave the way for my club. We made this decision together as a team.”

Sports.title: Harry Kane joins elite Champions League group with Cristiano Ronaldo as Bayern Munich add to stunning run
Sports.content:
Harry Kane joins elite Champions League group with Cristiano Ronaldo as Bayern Munich add to stunning run

Harry Kane scored in an eighth consecutive Champions League match as Bayern Munich beat Bodo/Glimt 5-0 in their league phase opener.

After assisting Jamal Musiala early on in the second half, Kane bagged their second of the night with a close-range header on 61 minutes.

3 Kane doubled the lead for Bayern as they thumped Bodo/Glimt Credit: Getty

The goal was his 55th in the Champions League and came on his 71st competition outing.

However, more impressively, Kane has become one of four players to score in eight or more consecutive matches in the competition.

He has followed Cristiano Ronaldo and Robert Lewandowski, who did so on two occasions each, as well as Ruud van Nistelrooy.

Kane goals in last eight Champions League matches September 10 - One goal vs Bodo/Glimt - League phase May 6 - One goal vs Paris Saint-Germain - Semi-final second leg April 28 - One goal vs Paris Saint-Germain - Semi-final first leg April 15 - One goal vs Real Madrid - Quarter-final second leg April 7 - One goal vs Real Madrid - Quarter-final first leg March 18 - Two goals vs Atalanta - Last 16 second leg January 28 - One goal vs PSV Eindhoven - League phase January 21 - Two goals vs Royale Union Saint-Gilloise - League phase

Bayern have won their opening match in the Champions League for a 23rd straight season, scoring 68 goals and conceding only eight.

Alphonso Davies scored their third of the night before a double from Michael Olise wrapped it up late on.

Bodo/Glimt went down to ten men with three minutes remaining in normal time when Odin Bjortuft saw red for a last-man foul.

How many goals has Kane scored this season?

After netting 61 times in all competitions last season, Kane has had a relatively slow start by his impressive standards.

The England captain scored on his third appearance of the campaign when Bayern beat VfL Osnabruck 4-1 in the DFB-Pokal.

Kane's header against Bodo/Glimt has taken him to three goals in five matches for 2026/27 thus far.

All that's missing is a goal in the Bundesliga, in which he was the top scorer during the previous campaign with 36.

3 Kane has found the back of the net in eight straight Champions League matches Credit: Getty

3 He has joined Ronaldo, as well as Lewandowski and Van Nistelrooy in the elite group Credit: Getty

He played that majority of the 5-1 win over Stuttgart, but was a surprise substitute in the 0-0 draw with Schalke.

Kane is now on a whopping total of 149 goals for Bayern, and could be heading towards Ballon d'Or glory.

The 33-year-old is one of 30 nominees for this year's award and a favourite to win football's most prestigious individual prize.

Who do Bayern play in the Champions League?

Norwegian side Viking FK host six-time winners Bayern in the next stage of the league phase on October 13.

Back-to-back tests against Arsenal and Atletico Madrid follow, with Lille and Slavia Prague their last two opponents in 2026.

At the beginning of 2027, it's Manchester United and Real Betis who complete their league phase schedule.

Sports.title: Champions League manager immediately resigns minutes after opening match
Sports.content:
Fenerbahce manager Ismail Kartal announced that he has resigned moments after his side's Champions League opener.

Kartal, who was only appointed in June, confirmed he would be leaving in his post-match press conference.

2 Kartal quit his job just minutes after the full time whistle in the Champions League Credit: Getty

The Turkish giants had just drawn at home to Roma in their first match of the league phase when he revealed the news.

“I am resigning from my position while there is still time," he said. "I am resigning with the understanding that I will never return.

“I have been here for three months. From the beginning of the season until today, the training sessions and camps I conducted with my players… our president and managers tried to help us in every way. Those were wonderful days.

"As of this evening, I congratulate my players and I am resigning from my position.

“Therefore, I would like to thank all my fans, media members, staff, and fellow players who have supported me until today.

“I made this decision to pave the way for my club. We made this decision together as a team.”

Kartal has now ended his fourth spell in charge of Fenerbahce, having taken charge in 2014, 2022, 2023 and earlier this year.

During his fourth spell, he only led the club into 11 games, winning six of them, drawing three and losing two, with one of the wins coming against Lyon last month, which ended in a chaotic brawl.

Fenerbahce's two losses had both come in the Turkish Super Lig though, meaning they are sitting ninth after four games.

And now, after failing to win in the Champions League, the 65-year-old has made the decision to depart.

2 Kartal revealed that he and the team have decided that he will leave his post Credit: Getty

Player stunned by Kartal resignation

It appears Kartal didn't run this by his players with Fenerbahce goalscorer Archie Brown discovering the news while giving interviews to journalists post-match.

The English left-back cut a stunned figure when a Fenerbahce official revealed to him that Kartal had resigned, asking: "What do you mean he resigned?"

After it was explained Kartal announced his resignation in a press conference, a confused Brown enquired: "As what? As coach?"

Wondering if things had been lost in translation, Brown asked: "What do you mean, resigned? He's not the coach any more?"

Resigned to the news of Kartal resigning was true, a shell-shocked Brown finished by saying: "I didn't know about this."

Leaving with a point

Kartal dropped the bombshell news straight after his side drew 1-1 with Serie A side Roma in Istanbul.

Bryan Cristante scored the opener for the visitors in the 39th minute, with them taking their lead into half time.

But Birmingham-born Brown equalised just after the break and neither side could then find a winner.

Fenerbahce's line-up included six-time Premier League winners with Manchester City Ederson and Nathan Ake, World Cup winner N'Golo Kante and ex-Manchester United winger Mason Greenwood.

Romelu Lukaku was also introduced as a late substitute, but he was unable to find the winning goal for his side.

Fenerbahce will now be looking to bring in a new boss ahead of their league game against Gaziantep on Sunday evening.

Their next European outing sees them travel to Aston Villa on October 14. Fenerbahce host Liverpool later in the league phase on November 4.

Sports.title: West Ham midfielder Edson Alvarez furiously rejects allegations he was involved in a kidnapping plot
Sports.content:
West Ham's Edson Alvarez has released a statement denying allegations that he was involved in a kidnapping plot.

Reports in his native Mexico claimed that he was involved in the crime that was allegedly ordered by his father-in-law.



3 Alvarez has angrily denied allegations that he was involved in a kidnapping Credit: Getty

However, he has now posted on social media to furiously reject the accusation, saying it has 'nothing to do' with him.

The 28-year-old midfielder slammed the claims and revealed that he has told his legal team to take the appropriate action.

Alvarez rejects allegations in statement

He wrote: “In light of the publications and statements that have circulated recently, I believe it is necessary to address this matter clearly and firmly.



“I categorically reject any allegation or attempt to associate my name with events, conflicts, or conduct that are entirely unrelated to me.

“Over the past several months, my name and image have repeatedly been used to generate greater media attention around a situation that has nothing to do with me.



“Until now, I had chosen not to respond.

"However, there are limits, and attributing knowledge, responsibility, or involvement in matters of this nature to me without presenting a single piece of evidence clearly crosses that line.

“If anyone believes they have evidence of any wrongdoing on my part, there are authorities, prosecutors, and courts before which they can present it.



“Serious accusations must be supported by evidence and presented before the appropriate authorities, not through statements in media outlets whose content prioritises sensationalism and media exposure over accuracy and truth.

“I will not allow my name to be used to fuel conflicts between third parties or to gain media exposure.

3 Alvarez posted the lengthy statement on social media following the claims Credit: @edsonnalvarez Instagram

“Therefore, given the seriousness of the statements that have been made, I have instructed my legal team to evaluate and pursue the appropriate legal action against any person who makes or disseminates false allegations against me.



“I also want to be clear regarding the publications that have attempted to connect me to this matter through my former partner’s father: It is not my place to confirm, deny, or comment on what may be said about third parties, but it is my responsibility to make one thing absolutely clear: I have nothing to do with the events being reported.

“Throughout nearly ten years of my professional career, I have made every effort to stay away from media scandals and to have my name recognised for my work both on and off the pitch.

“I come from a hardworking and honourable family that taught me that a reputation is built over many years through hard work, discipline, and conduct.

“For that very reason, I will not allow mine to be irresponsibly used to involve me in matters that are entirely unrelated to me.



“My priority is, and will continue to be, where it has always been: my daughters, my family, and my professional career.”

3 Alvarez has only played one game for West Ham so far this season Credit: Getty

Alvarez followed up the statement with a picture of him playing for West Ham earlier this season against Portsmouth.

That was his only appearance of the campaign so far for the Hammers, as he played 75 minutes in the Carabao Cup.



The Mexico international, who captained his country at the World Cup in the summer, has made 74 appearances in total for the club since joining from Ajax in 2023.

Sports.title: 15-year-old wonderkid makes Manchester United history with stunning debut hat-trick
Sports.content:
Manchester United wonderkid JJ Gabriel scored a hat-trick on his UEFA Youth League debut on Thursday afternoon.

Gabriel, who has been playing for Man United's U21 side aged just 15, is arguably the hottest prospect in world football.

2 Gabriel scored a hat-trick for Man United's U19s against Sabah on Thursday Credit: Getty

Red Devils icon Ryan Giggs labelled him a 'generational talent' earlier this week, and the teenager has now shown why.

United's U19s beat Sabah 5-0 ahead of the first teams' Champions League clash, which is live on talkSPORT, with Gabriel scoring three.

And by doing so, he made history for the Premier League giants.

At 15 years and 339 days old, he is now the youngest ever goalscorer for the club in the UEFA Youth League, overtaking Angel Gomes, who netted in the competition aged 17 and 34 days old.

Gabriel's historic hat-trick

Gabriel scored his first of the game just before half time, as he perfectly volleyed in a rebound to make it 3-0.

A shot bounced back to him, forcing him to react quickly and chest the ball down, finding the back of the net with his laces.

His second, which came in the 85th minute of the match, saw him take one touch in the box, neatly cut inside onto his right foot, and tuck a strike into the bottom corner.

Gabriel's third came just two minutes after, as Jim Thwaites' lofted ball sent the young star racing through on goal.

He then brushed off some pressure from the chasing defenders and broke into the box, smashing past the goalkeeper.

The rising talent wheeled off to celebrate and then held three fingers aloft with the match ball after the whistle.

2 Gabriel has been labelled a generational talent and could be nearing a first-team debut Credit: Getty

When could Gabriel make his first-team debut?

Man United's Gabriel continues to show why he is considered one of the best young players on the planet.

So, after scoring a hat-trick on his Youth League debut, could that mean a first-team debut could be on the cards?

He made his first senior appearances for the Red Devils during pre-season and has regularly trained alongside Bruno Fernandes and co.

And manager Michael Carrick said in August: "JJ is one of the boys. He's obviously got a really big talent.

"He's trained with us quite a bit and is getting experience all the time. He's physically adapting to each step, and we're just continuing his development."

Should he be handed his full Man United debut before October 22, he would become the club's youngest-ever player.

Goalkeeper David Gaskell holds the record after playing his first game aged 16 years and 19 days.

Sports.title: Leicester warned they’re heading for ‘Armageddon’ as prospective new owner outlines plan to save them
Sports.content:
Leicester City are heading towards financial 'Armageddon' without fresh capital and improved results, says prospective owner Neil Lal.

The Scottish-Indian businessman, who is president of the Indian Council of the United Kingdom, is fronting a group to try and buy Leicester.

6 Lal has issued a stark warning over Leicester's finances amid a potential takeover Credit: Neil Lal - Linkedin

Lal's Bharat Consortium Group has three other investors, each also seeking 25 per cent of the club, with significant backing from India.

"We are all wealthy businessmen," said Lal, speaking exclusively to talkSPORT. "Rather than going through the bankers of Leicester City Football Club, we have contacted the board directly, which saves time. We have made an offer.

"It is now a waiting game, but we are in contact with the club, which is a positive... our key objective is financial stability from the start."

talkSPORT understands Lal has contacted the club but has not yet spoken to Top or other senior members of the board. Leicester has set a deadline of September 14 for initial offers from interested parties, and there are at least three active groups in the process.

Saudi executive Turki Alalshikh has also been sounded out following his decision in August to pull out of buying Derby County, Leicester's east midlands rivals.

Leicester owner Aiyawatt 'Top' Srivaddhanaprabha is seeking over £200million and, according to Lal, any new owner would also have to assume significant debt on top of that price.

Leicester warned of more financial woes

"In my view, the club is overvalued," Lal, one of the leading voices promoting Scotland-India trade, explained. "Leicester is valued as a successful Championship club, and yet it's in League One. So, for me, the valuation is over the top.

"The second point is, the debt is a major concern, and the future liabilities. We have got to look at the books. That's important.

"I hope I am wrong, but I fear if something is not done quickly there could be more financial struggles ahead for Leicester."

Leicester have tasked investment banking firm CitiGroup with finding a new owner.

6 Saudi boxing chief Alalshikh is understood to have been sounded out over a purchase Credit: Getty

An eight-page pitch deck, seen by talkSPORT, emphasises Leicester's history and facilities, and stresses the appeal of investing in the 'third-largest English city with only one (football) club'.

Leicester's fall from grace

A decade ago, the Foxes won a fairytale Premier League title under Claudio Ranieri at pre-season odds of 5000/1. Yet, they now find themselves in League One and have won only one of their opening five league games under new manager Russell Martin.

The weekend's 4-0 loss to Oxford United was a new low, and some Foxes fans have called for Martin to be sacked.

"That defeat was not good," said Lal. "It was very disappointing. It doesn't bode well for the club.

"I'd rather not say too much because, as you can appreciate, it will affect outcomes, but I understand the manager was with Rangers at one point, and he left there.

"Obviously things are not going well at Leicester at the moment but we've got to be positive. Hopefully, things turn around. What I will say, though, is we are people of zero tolerance, and we are here for the long term."

6 Leicester have suffered turmoil on and off the pitch, and now play in the third tier Credit: Getty

Lal sees appeal in Leicester's storied past, but admits the Foxes must come to terms with their perilous present. He also believes Leicester's multi-cultural community is a huge asset, and that the thriving Indian population can be better engaged with.

Lal has aspirations to promote and commercialise Leicester in India where, as former Premier League winners, the club is already well known.

"Leicester winning the Premier League (in 2015/16) was probably one of the greatest sporting triumphs of all time," he said. "If someone said to me in 2014, Leicester is going to win the league, I'd have thought, 'Okay, listen, they've had too much to drink. Go and see a doctor!'

"Winning the Premier League and the (2020/21) FA Cup, and doing well in Europe, was fantastic. And Leicester has a great set of loyal fans.

"There is potential there. And yet there's many things we've got to do to make things better. We've got to be profitable. We've got to have financial stability. We've got to think about winning. That's the key thing.

"We have also got to respect the tradition of what's happened, and the late owner (Khun Vichai), Top and the whole (Srivaddhanaprabha) family.

"This is not a quick fix by just throwing the kitchen sink at it. This is a long-term strategy. It's a five-year plan to get Leicester back to the Championship and then the Premier League, and we don't just want to go up a division only to come back down again after a year."

Lal's comments echo a recent statement by the Foxes Trust which called on Leicester City to "reassure supporters on the financial health and viability of the club until a sale has taken place".

6 Leicester were crowned as Premier League champions just a decade ago Credit: AFP or licensors

Lal's consortium are open to putting a fan representative on the board and also plan to consult several Leicester legends on key club decisions.

"I'll definitely consider that (putting a fan on the board)," said Lal. "I understand where the Foxes Trust are coming from and I agree with many of their points.

"There has got to be community and fan engagement. We have got to listen to the fans. This is vital. Without the fans, we are nothing. And I think having a committee of maybe six to eight ex-Leicester footballers to discuss the buying and selling of players would be a good thing.

"I'm a numbers person. I just want the club to be financially viable and profitable. But regarding recruiting players or picking managers, I think we should leave that to the experts to come back to us with suggestions. That'll be the best way."

Several investors contacted by talkSPORT believe a sale is not just desired by Top but required. There is a danger without one Leicester are heading towards administration, which comes with an automatic 12-point deduction.

The challenge for Lal, and other interested parties contacted by talkSPORT, is Leicester are yet to share the full financial picture of the club making future liabilities hard to predict before undertaking the rigorous due diligence process.

This may be down to CitiGroup wishing to whittle down a shortlist of viable owners first, which is a normal step, or even a hope of jumping straight to a preferred bidder, who would then traditionally be handed an exclusive period to comb through the books.

talkSPORT has learned at least two groups have walked away from the process due to concerns over the club's debt from the limited financial information already provided. Lal's own fear is that results on the field decline further before he has a chance to influence the club.

6 Martin is already under pressure as the new Leicester boss amid poor results Credit: Getty

"If we're going to progress further, and Leicester is falling down (the table), it doesn't bode well," said Lal, who has no plans to sell off the club's Seagrave training centre or the 32,259-capacity King Power Stadium. "If, God forbid, Leicester ever drops down to League Two, financially, it's Armageddon. It really is.

"Right now, we have a club that has a huge wage bill and debts, and it's in League One. That's a concern.

"My fear is if this continues for the long term, over the next two-four months, and Leicester's not playing well in the league, then unfortunately, we are going to have to review the situation and possibly walk. And I don't want to do that...

"The foundations are there, but the problem is the financial stability is not. In my humble opinion, I think the club has been a bit mismanaged."

Leicester is not the only club Lal is looking at. He is also open to investing in Rangers. Although the Foxes are his primary focus, building a multi-club network is not discounted.

"Rangers are going through a bit of a tough patch at the moment," said Lal. "New owners [Andrew Cavenagh and 49rs Enterprises] have taken over and, obviously, they need time, but there's also financial losses. So at the end of the day, if the opportunity arises and we can come to the right price, we may look at the situation.

"Unfortunately, in Scotland, the [country's] coefficient ranking has dropped, which impacts European qualification, adding extra playoff rounds.

"Rangers have huge support. It's a wonderful club. If the opportunity arises, we may look at it. It's Leicester right now, and then if Rangers ever comes up, let's see what happens."

6 Leicester could have new ownership by the end of 2026 Credit: Getty

Lal will not be afraid to make difficult decisions if successful in buying Leicester, but he is also keen to protect the legacy of both King Power and the Srivaddhanaprabha family.

Part of the reason he has made a direct offer to the club, bypassing CitiGroup, is a belief that dealing directly with Top stands the best possible chance of agreeing a deal, and persuading the Leicester owner to lower his asking price.

"I have total respect for Top and his late father," said Lal. "They have put a lot of money into the club. Unfortunately, financially, the club's not doing great right now. But we've got to respect that remarkable 5,000/1 win... I can assure you no one wants to erode and disrespect that legacy.

"Top and his family, for me, are Leicester royalty, and they should always be part of the club... But we've got to be truthful as well. Integrity, character, morals, and principles are the four key points I'll always adhere to.

"Without financial stability, we can't move forward. The problem is, and this is not only with Leicester but across many football clubs, you can't just lose money year after year. This is why you have many clubs going to Administration, and some have actually closed completely. We can't have that with Leicester."

It's a worrying time for Foxes fans, both on and off the field, but sources have told talkSPORT the intent is to have a new owner in place before the season ends, and potentially even by the end of this year.

Leicester were approached for comment.

Sports.title: Hakim Ziyech finds new club four days after ex-Chelsea star had contract terminated
Sports.content:
Hakim Ziyech finds new club four days after ex-Chelsea star had contract terminated

Former Chelsea forward Hakim Ziyech has signed for Brazilian giants Botafogo on a free transfer.

Ziyech had only been without a club since Sunday, when his contract with Moroccan club Wydad was terminated.

2 Ex-Chelsea star Ziyech has signed for Botafogo days after terminating his contract Credit: Getty

The 33-year-old winger departed after 11 months, having played 16 games and scored nine goals, assisting two.

But he has now made an instant move to Brazil, signing a two-year deal with Botafogo on Thursday.

Botafogo officially announced the move on social media, writing: "Hakim Ziyech is with BOTAFOGO.

"World Cup player and multi-champion in Europe, the attacking midfielder signs with the Glorious One until the end of 2028."

Why did Hakim Ziyech leave Wydad?

Ziyech, who won the Champions League with Chelsea in 2021, received thanks from Wydad after leaving the club.

A mutual agreement was reached to rip up his contract, seemingly to allow him to make a move elsewhere for free.

Wydad wrote: "Sometimes, some stories are shorter than we had hoped, but they leave a mark that cannot be erased.

"You were one of us, and you will always remain part of the Wydad Athletic family.

"From the Wydad of the nation, we say thank you for every moment in which you wore the club's shirt, and we wish you every success and good fortune in your coming career, on the pitch and off it.

"Some journeys may come to an end, but the memories remain, and Wydad will always have a place in your heart. Thank you, Hakim, for being part of our story."

2 Ziyech has played for Galatasaray, Al-Duhail and Wydad since leaving Chelsea in 2023 Credit: Getty

Who else plays for Botafogo?

Ziyech, who chipped in with six goals and nine assists from 34 English top-flight matches between 2020-2023, will now be playing alongside some fellow former Premier League stars.

Ex-Manchester United defender Alex Telles, former Everton midfielder Allan and ex-Nottingham Forest star Danilo are all part of the squad that the Moroccan has joined.

Jesse Lingard is also playing in the Brazilian Serie A with Corinthians, while Jadon Sancho has been linked with the league too.

Ziyech's old Chelsea teammate Thiago Silva, Andreas Pereira and Memphis Depay are just some of the other former Premier League players competing in the division.

And of course, Brazil icon Neymar still plays in his home nation.

Ziyech could make his Botafogo debut against RB Bragantino on Saturday, with kick-off at midnight in the UK.

Sports.title: Lionesses legend Jill Scott handed new job at EFL club
Sports.content:
Jill Scott has been appointed chief women's football advisor by Salford City.

The former England midfielder is set to work with the women's first-team and academy at the Ammies.



3 Scott has made a return to football with League Two Salford Credit: Getty

It marks a return to football for Scott following her retirement in 2022.

The 39-year-old has since launched a media career which includes punditry on The Overlap alongside Gary Neville, Jamie Carragher, Roy Keane and Ian Wright.

She has now joined Salford, who are owned by a group which includes Neville and David Beckham.



Whilst the men's first-team play in League Two, the club's women's side are in the sixth tier of English football.

Salford City Lionesses have won their opening two matches of the season in the North West Women's Regional League Division One Central.



Their first match following Scott's arrival as an advisor comes at home to Bury on Sunday.

Scott joins Salford City

Speaking to the club's media channels, she explained: "I’m incredibly excited to be stepping into this new role, helping to drive the Lionesses forward and achieve our powerful ambitions.



"With the backing and knowledge of AIG, and a team of passionate, talented people at Salford, I have no doubt that the years ahead will be some of our most memorable yet."

In addition to Scott's appointment, Salford have also welcomed investment from AIG.

The American insurance firm have become the Lionesses' largest minority equity investor.

3 Neville and Beckham joined forces to help propel Salford up the English divisions Credit: Getty



AIG's executive vice chairman Ed Dandridge has hailed the arrival of Scott, adding: "We applaud the appointment of Jill Scott as chief women’s football advisor for Salford City.

"Jill is an incredibly decorated player and trailblazer in professional football who will serve as a tremendous source of technical instruction and inspiration to Salford City’s women’s and men’s teams as we move forward together on this exciting journey."

Scott's playing career

As a player, Scott won 161 caps for England, scoring 26 goals for the Lionesses.

She was part of the side which won the Women's Euros in 2022, going viral for an X-rated tirade at Germany's Sydney Lohmann.



Scott was also in the squad which reached the final of the Women's Euros in 2009 and the England side which finished third at the 2015 Women's World Cup in Canada.

Her career included eight major tournament finals with the Lionesses as well as two Olympic Games as part of Team GB.

3 Salford City Lionesses currently play in the sixth tier of English women's football Credit: Shutterstock Editorial

At club level, Scott won nine trophies across her time at Everton and Manchester City, including a Women's Super League title in 2016.



The Sunderland-born star also had spells with the Black Cats and Aston Villa during her career.

Sports.title: ESPN under-fire over 'unprofessional' botched US Open graphic of Serena and Venus Williams
Sports.content:
Tennis fans were furious to see a botched ESPN graphic that was supposed to include photos of both Venus and Serena Williams.

'I think ESPN just threw up a graphic using two pictures of Serena????' one eagle-eyed fan wrote on X. 'Whoops.'

The graphic was intended to depict the five American women of the Open Era with the most victories in major singles matches before their 23rd birthday.

That list is topped by Venus Williams at 107, thanks to a professional career that began when she was just 14. Serena, who also turned pro at 14, ranked second with 103 wins before turning 23, followed by Mary Joe Fernandez (93), Chris Evert (90) and Coco Gauff (89).

Unfortunately for ESPN, Venus was not pictured. Instead, the graphic included two different photos of Serena alongside the images of Fernandez, Evert and Gauff.

'[ESPN] please do better,' one fan wrote on X. 'This is unprofessional.'

Tennis fans were furious to see a botched ESPN graphic during the ongoing US Open

Serena (right) and Venus (left) lost their first-round doubles match at Flushing Meadows

'For how bad ESPN is, they should be embarrassed over this,' another added on the r/tennis subreddit.

One fan joked that Ben Shelton's five-set quarterfinal win over reigning champion Carlos Alcaraz probably deprived ESPN's graphics department of any sleep. That match ended at 3.33am.

The Williams sisters were back in action at the US Open this year. Serena and Venus suffered defeat following a three-hour battle against Maya Joint and Chan Hao-ching in their first-round doubles matchup at the Grand Slam on Friday night.

In the wake of the loss, the 23-time Grand Slam champion wasn't sticking around to savor her return to Flushing Meadows.

Serena 'fled the scene' leaving her sister and playing partner behind, according to tennis insider Ben Rothenberg.

She reportedly walked off the Arthur Ashe court, out of the stadium and straight into a car that was waiting to whisk her away into the New York City night.

In her haste to escape, Serena is said to have ditched Venus, who had headed to the locker room post-match, as is customary for players.

What's more, Rothenberg reported that Venus may have been amenable to speaking to the media but instead, Serena's hasty exit saw the duo skip post-match press.

The superstar siblings were obligated to speak to the press following their grueling showdown against Joint and Chan after multiple members of the media requested them. However, tournament officials opted against fining either of the fabulously wealthy tennis legends.

Sports.title: How Patrick Dorgu fared on his left-back audition in Man United's win over Sabah: The key areas he needs to improve, where he is BETTER than Luke Shaw and what Michael Carrick learnt ahead of Man City clash
Sports.content:
How Patrick Dorgu fared on his left-back audition in Man United's win over Sabah: The key areas he needs to improve, where he is BETTER than Luke Shaw and what Michael Carrick learnt ahead of Man City clash

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

There was one sequence midway through the first half that perhaps best encapsulated the good and the bad of Patrick Dorgu the left back.

With the game locked at 0-0, Sabah broke on the counter and there was Dorgu, as far forward as any United player, appearing totally uninterested in sprinting back. It did not go unnoticed.

But then, seconds later, Sabah were dispossessed in the middle of the park, the ball was turned over and in a flash it was ferried out to Dorgu, still high and wide, to pick his head up and deliver a dead-eye cross to the near post for Matheus Cunha to score. Cunha immediately pointed at Dorgu in recognition of the quality of the assist. Pandemonium followed in the stands.

United's second goal owed a lot to Dorgu, too.

Youri Tielemans, who was brilliant before he went off at half-time, gave it to United's 'new' left back near the halfway line and he strode with purpose before playing it out to Cunha.

Dorgu overlapped, willingly as those are the positions he loves to take up, and Sabah's back-line had to hedge having seen the damage his crosses could do. That hesitation opened up a passing lane for Tielemans to receive and spin in the box, cut it back to Bruno Fernandes and up went the roar around Old Trafford when it nestled into the bottom corner.

Patrick Dorgu was awarded the PlayStation Player of the Match award up against FK Sabah

Dorgu was a constant threat in attack but showed signs of vulnerabilty when defending

So by the time the players filtered off the pitch, Dorgu had the UEFA Player of the Match trophy in his hands. A huge positive, even if Dorgu the left back remains very much a work in progress.

Before getting in to the specifics of where Dorgu must improve it's important to stress it was a night of huge positives in what many dubbed a left back audition. Those behind the scenes at United feel it can become something much more permanent.

There was something of an irony to the fact that Dorgu looked the most dangerous wide player on the pitch going forward, and yet somehow also looked capable of bringing the most danger to United's door going backwards.

Where Luke Shaw, missing from this clash due to the after-effects of cramp sustained at Everton - where he was brilliant - cannot sustain the attacking output that brings a whole new dimension to this team, elevating the likes of Cunha immeasurably, Dorgu can. And yet this man-of-the-match display still showed the Dane has plenty to do bring Shaw's level of calmness at the back.

For all the good here (and there was a lot) - for a start he had more touches in the box (8) and created more chances (3) than any other player on the pitch at half-time - a willing learner like Dorgu will come away with plenty to work on.

There were multiple moments where Dorgu over-committed, where Dorgu misjudged the press and where Dorgu appeared to have little appetite to do the defensive side of the game. He looked like a winger playing left back when the odd occasion arrived to defend.

When tougher assignments come up, he won't get bailed out. Lisandro Martinez told him as much in one rather tense first half exchange after being bypassed by Kaheem Parris.

Before coming off on 70 minutes he was beaten off his spot in a turnover and pulled down his man cynically for a booking. An acute reminder with Manchester City on the horizon.

The truth is that this is as new for Dorgu as it is for Carrick and his staff.

He arrived as a left back from Lecce who made his debut at right wing-back. When Ruben Amorim reluctantly went to a back four against Newcastle United on that infamous Boxing Day, he was pushed to a right-wing role.

Darren Fletcher, who held the fort as an interim between Amorim and Carrick, platformed him as a left winger and Carrick has mostly followed suit. His crossing is a real strength and his athleticism allows him to constantly provide an outlet out wide. That much is largely undeniable.

But then United didn't get a left back this summer. They couldn't get Lewis Hall out of Newcastle United and they can't expect Shaw to play twice a week. His 'rest day' on Wednesday was evidence enough of that.

Dorgu was key to unlocking Matheus Cunha (left) and there was a point of appreciation after Dorgu's cross to Cunha allowed United to open the scoring on Thursday night

So, United need to invest in Dorgu as a left back. Between now and January, or now and the end of the season, United will be a far stronger unit with Dorgu hitting all the right notes at both ends from left back.

They have Marcus Rashford who can play left wing. They have Cunha, too. What they don't have is an abundance of left backs and that is why Dorgu must become more than just a European experiment.

Against a Sabah side that targeted Dorgu's side much more so than Noussair Mazraoui on the opposite flank, Carrick and his staff can be forgiven for asking Dorgu to stay high and wide in a bid to overload at the top end of the pitch. This was a one-sided contest for the most part.

Tougher tests will come, particularly so this weekend if Shaw is not fit enough to start against Manchester City back here at Old Trafford on Sunday afternoon. A lack of intensity in your defensive duties against Antoine Semenyo or Iliman Ndiaye is very different, with all due respect, to doing so against Parris and Co.

Some of it was effort, some of it was tactical and positional. If Carrick and his staff want Dorgu to play as high as they did here, the left centre back, in this case Martinez, needs more protection. At times the gaps were glaring.

But a 4-0 rout of a European minnow is a good time to try something new and Dorgu came through it with a trophy in his hands.

Carrick said this week that Dorgu can be 'like a new signing' and any new signing would need time to adapt.

Here was Dorgu playing left back for the first time under Carrick and playing in the Champions League for the first time, too. He needs time to learn and adapt.

Some of the defensive problems were down to effort and others were down to the tactics

The good: Dorgu helped unlock the team in attack, helping Cunha to produce his best performance of the season and create extra space for Fernandes and Tielemans to operate in. The bad: he forgot to lock the door at the other end in an up-and-done first 45.

How Dorgu kicks on from here will have a huge bearing on the left back recruitment for January and next summer.

The fundamentals are all there and team-mates are elevated in their proper positions when a left back in Dorgu's mould enters the fold. So much of playing him there makes sense.

So, is the long term answer at left back actually already in the building?

Only Dorgu can prove whether or not he's the man to succeed Shaw for more than just the visit of Sabah.

Sports.title: Pakistan endure another day of despair as miserable tour continues: This once great cricketing nation has been reduced to chaos and cluelessness as England close in on series whitewash, writes LAWRENCE BOOTH
Sports.content:
Moments after Ollie Robinson, immovable from the crest of his wave, had Saim Ayub caught in the slips by Harry Brook from the first ball of Pakistan’s second innings, a PA announcement warned Edgbaston stewards of a ‘Code Red’.

It had apparently been triggered by a fire alarm and, for a few seconds, the crowd fell eerily silent. But they burst into life three balls later when Robinson had Abdullah Shafique poking low to Joe Root at first slip, leaving the tourists nought for two and facing a Code Red situation of their own.

The fire alarm proved false, and Pakistan saved at least a little face by reaching 52 for two before rain ended play shortly after 5pm.

But as Root’s team closed in on a 3–0 whitewash in gloomy Birmingham, it was possible to feel two emotions at the same time: delight for England, who batted with panache and bowled with precision, and despair for Pakistan, a once great side reduced to chaos and cluelessness by the machinations of their board and the misery of their players.

There was uproar in Karachi and Lahore when, only two days into this series, their side were described as the worst their country had sent to these shores for 50 years. Those voices have fallen silent now, with England – in disarray themselves not long ago – largely doing as they pleased on the second day of this third and final Test.

Resuming on 156 for four, they thrashed 297 in 60 overs before being dismissed for 453, at which point Robinson took his series haul to 21 wickets at an average of 6.66 with the kind of precision that turns metronomes green with envy. It has all been closer to bloodsport than sport.

Ollie Robinson shone again as England closed in on a series whitewash over Pakistan

It was another day of despair for Pakistan as their miserable tour of England nears an end

We should be careful what we wish for, of course. Until recently, the idea of England winning every Test of a series would have been greeted with a snort of derision. But while they deserve credit for keeping their foot on Pakistan’s throat, the one-sidedness of the cricket has raised more questions about a format that rarely stops fretting over its future.

It’s no good grumbling about the unfettered growth of the T20 franchise circuit when Test cricket is properly contested by only a handful of nations. And it’s no good wondering why this inequality has been allowed to arise when the bigger nations shrug their shoulders at the ICC’s lopsided financial model, and the ICC themselves turn a blind eye to the game’s growing politicisation.

As this tour has confirmed, Pakistan are on the wrong side of each of these debates, with the chairman of their cricket board, Mohsin Naqvi, doubling up as the country’s interior minister, and presiding over the farcical culling of almost half their squad between Lord’s and Edgbaston.

It all meant the day proceeded along predictable lines, with Harry Brook and Dan Lawrence sniffing out any prospect of a Pakistani comeback by taking 73 from the morning’s first 10 overs while barely breaking sweat.

But if there has been one criticism of England, it has been the failure of their batsmen to convert starts into something more meaningful, and here again they promised more than they delivered.

Brook had struck the perfect tempo in moving to 75 in three and a quarter hours when he pushed an off-break from Ayub towards midwicket and set off for a single even as Shan Masood swooped on the ball, before running him out comfortably at the non-striker’s end.

Might Lawrence reach three figures instead? Moments before lunch, he contrived to chop a widish delivery from Mohammad Imran on to his stumps, and walked off in anguish for 65. Three half-centuries in four innings since his recall have been a good return, but the battle for top-six places is cranking up. This was an opportunity missed.

Jamie Smith, batting with a dislocated left index finger sustained in the field on the first day, played some meaty strokes for his third sixty in five innings, only to provide a simple return catch off a leading edge to Razaullah.

And while Robinson hit out for his second Test fifty, his dismissal left England with 21 half-centuries from six games this summer, and a lone hundred, by Ben Duckett against New Zealand at Trent Bridge.

Unless one of Pakistan’s batsmen can go big tomorrow, this will be the first Test series in England of three matches or more not to feature an individual century since the 1888 Ashes.

Harry Brook and Dan Lawrence were two of five England batsmen to pass 50 in their innings

This Pakistan side are one of the worst touring teams to ever come to here for a Test series

Not that any of this troubled Robinson as he performed his now customary demolition of Pakistan’s top order.

Ayub’s most recent cricket had been for Jamaica Kingsmen in the Caribbean Premier League, which most sensible set-ups might think was no kind of preparation for red-ball cricket under grey English skies. Sure enough, he completed a pair by wafting hopelessly at his first ball.

Cox, keeping in place of the injured Smith, now came up to the stumps for Shafique, who poked at Robinson as if in a trance. Since making 61 at Headingley, Shafique has managed 23 in five innings, and been dismissed in five of his six by Robinson.

Duckett put down a slip catch for the third time in the game when Shan Masood flashed at the luckless Gus Atkinson, while Jofra Archer lacked his usual menace. But such is the gulf between the sides that England can afford these blemishes and still win this game at a canter.

Sports.title: Dan Lawrence says Ollie Robinson is 'at the peak of his powers' after England bowler continues remarkable series against Pakistan - and gives verdict on own position in team
Sports.content:
Ollie Robinson is operating at the ‘peak of his powers’ and making his England team-mates believe he will take a wicket every ball.

That was the assessment from the slip cordon of Dan Lawrence, after Robinson struck twice in the opening over of Pakistan’s second innings at Edgbaston.

‘When he's bowling, when he's putting it in the same spot pretty much every ball, you certainly do feel in the game behind the stumps, especially when you've got someone pretty much at the peak of his powers,’ said Lawrence.

Robinson’s double strike took his series wickets tally to an astonishing 21 at a cost of just 6.66 runs each.

Bad weather ended play prematurely, leaving a Pakistan team yet to make 200 in five previous innings on 52 for two and requiring 268 more runs to make Joe Root’s England bat again.

At the other end of the day, Surrey’s Lawrence dominated the early scoring in a rapid start alongside Harry Brook, but like his fifth-wicket partner failed to turn a half century into a hundred, finishing with 65 off 82 balls, in a score of 453.

Dan Lawrence heaped praise on Ollie Robinson after he continued his remarkable series

Lawrence, who earlier scored 65, said the England bowler was 'at the peak of his powers'

With three 50s in four innings, the 29-year-old might have done enough to maintain his place in the squad for the winter tour of South Africa. Jacob Bethell will be back from knee surgery by then and Sam Curran has been nominated as Ben Stokes’ successor in the all-rounder role. The rest will be determined over the next fortnight.

Incoming coach Stephen Fleming is scheduled to arrive next week and is understood to be keen on getting around the country, talking to directors of cricket and coaches about the country’s leading players.

‘In regards to position in the team, only the selectors and the captain will know that, and I'm pretty happy with how I've contributed and we'll see what happens,’ Lawrence said.

‘I felt like I was playing really nicely and it was a really good surface to bat on against a tiring attack. I thought I was going to make a really big score to be honest, but it wasn't meant to be.’

Surrey team-mate Jamie Smith and Robinson also made half centuries, although the former was unable to take his place behind the stumps due to a dislocated finger.

Jordan Cox will keep wicket for the remainder of a contest that appears destined to finish on Friday, marking the beginning of the post-Bazball era with a 3-0 whitewash.

Sports.title: Six Nations matches in the USA! World Rugby say they want to host flagship games across the pond
Sports.content:
Six Nations matches in the USA! World Rugby say they want to host flagship games across the pond

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

World Rugby are pushing for the Six Nations to stage a money-spinning Test in America.

A sell-out crowd is expected for Saturday's clash between South Africa and New Zealand in Baltimore as the sport tries to open new markets.

The USA will host the 2031 World Cup and the sport's governing body believe there is enough appetite to stage a Stateside Six Nations fixture.

'In terms of the match-day economics, South Africa vs New Zealand is like a Six Nations match,' said World Rugby CEO Alan Gilpin.

'If you could take a Six Nations game to the right place, to a Boston or to a New York, where there's a lot of those fanbases, you can definitely drive the economics,

'I've used the example before… only as an example… of an Italy vs Ireland game. You've got two fantastic fan bases in the US of Irish and Italian fans.

World Rugby are pushing for the Six Nations to stage a money-spinning Test in America

'Now, you're going to have Irish fans and Italian fans in those respective home countries saying, "Hang on a minute, you know, we want to see our country play?"

'The counter argument to that [is] it's still Irish and Italian fans getting the chance to watch their team, so they're just not the ones who live in Ireland and Italy on this occasion. But that's a balancing piece we've got to work through.'

Sports.title: Baseball icon and Hiroshima atomic bomb survivor Isao Harimoto dies aged 86
Sports.content:
Baseball legend Isao Harimoto, who survived the atomic bombing of Hiroshima, has died aged 86.

The Korean-Japanese icon, who was born in Hiroshima in 1940 to Korean parents who migrated to Japan during the country's rule of Korea, died in Tokyo on Wednesday.

Growing up, he overcame huge adversity as a child. Firstly he was involved in an accident in 1944 that left him with severe burns on his right hand.

The result of that left him with limited mobility in his thumb and forefinger, while his middle three fingers became permanently curled.

Then a year later, he survived the United States of America's atomic bombing of Hiroshima during World War II on August 6, 1945.

Harimoto, whose birth name was Jang Hun, survived after his mother used her body to shield him and one of his sisters from the blast. However, sadly another sister did not survive. Between 60,000 and 80,000 people were killed instantly - with the final death toll calculated at 135,000.

Korean-Japanese baseball legend Isao Harimoto died aged 86 in Tokyo on Wednesday

Known as the 'Hit Machine' he recorded the most hits in Japanese baseball history at 3,085

After a difficult childhood, Harimoto later turned his attention to baseball. He had to learn to play left-handed due to his injuries and wore a custom glove to fit his injured right hand that allowed him to catch the ball.

But despite those hindrances, Harimoto enjoyed a distinguished 23-year career - playing for Toei Flyers, the Yomiuri Giants and the Lotte Orions across his homeland. At the Flyers he helped them win their first Japan Series in 1962.

Known as the 'Hit Machine' he recorded the most hits in Japanese baseball history at 3,085 and is the only player in Nippon Professional Baseball League (NPB) to surpass the 3,000 landmark.

Furthermore he is the only player in NPB history to hit over 500 home runs and steal more than 300 bases - with his figures at 504 and 319 respectively. By comparison, only three players in Major League Baseball history have achieved the same feat in Barry Bonds, Willie Mays and Alex Rodriguez.

An 18-time All-Star, he was inducted into the Japanese Baseball Hall of Fame in 1990.

The Golden Players Club, one of Japan’s two halls of fame, wrote: 'All members of the Meikyukai express our deep respect and gratitude for Mr Isao Harimoto’s many years of great achievements, and we sincerely pray [following] his passing.'

Sports.title: Boxing Day bonanza is back with SEVEN games as Premier League confirm TV dates for festive period - following last season's backlash with just one fixture played
Sports.content:
The Premier League has confirmed that seven games will be staged on Boxing Day after releasing its latest set of fixtures. Four games will be held at 3pm, with Aston Villa facing Leeds at 12.30pm, Hull taking on Liverpool at 5.30pm, before Newcastle host Manchester City at 8pm. A triple header follows on Super Sunday on Sky Sports on December 27, with Chelsea facing Coventry at 2pm, Man United hosting Nottingham Forest at 4.30pm and Crystal Palace taking on champions Arsenal at 7pm. It comes after the league faced widespread backlash after hosting just one game on Boxing Day - one of the most popular dates on the football calendar - last year. That will kick off a busy schedule over the festive season, with three further rounds of matches to be held over the period up to January 7. A round of midweek evening fixtures will take place on December 29 and December 30, before Leeds host Everton in the only game on New Year's Day. Boxing Day football is back in the Premier League with seven fixtures confirmed Last year, Man United vs Newcastle was the only fixture that was scheduled on Boxing Day The rest of that gameweek will take place on January 2 and January 3, before the festive schedule concludes with a round of games that will fall from January 5 to January 7. Every fixture from the December 29 to December 30 round and the one from January 5 to January 7 will be broadcast on Sky Sports The early announcement comes after the Premier League consulted broadcast partners, the Football Supporters' Association and representatives from club Fan Advisory Boards. There is a desire to give as much notice as possible for those travelling to games. As part of the schedule, each club is guaranteed at least a 60-hour break between matches in order to help them deal with the fixture congestion. The early announcement is likely to be welcomed by fans after the Premier League was heavily criticised for arranging just one game on Boxing Day last season. Manchester United vs Newcastle was the only match, with the top flight blaming scheduling issues caused by European football and the Carabao Cup. At the time, they said: 'There are now several challenges to Premier League fixture scheduling rooted in the expansion of European club competitions – which led to a revision of our domestic calendar ahead of last season, including changes to the FA Cup. 'This ultimately left the Premier League as a 33-weekend competition – fewer than previous seasons, despite being a 380-match competition since 1995. 'With fewer weekends to work with, the league is bound by how the calendar falls. 'The league can give an assurance that next season there will be more Premier League matches on Boxing Day – as the date falls on a Saturday.'
