Sports.title: Musical Times storms to the head of the betting for next year's 1,000 Guineas with scintillating display... plus our top tips for Day Two of the St Leger Festival
Sports.content:
Musical Times stormed to the head of the betting for next year's 1,000 Guineas with a scintillating display in the Group 2 Betfred May Hill Stakes at Doncaster.

A smooth winner of her first two starts at Newmarket and Yarmouth, the daughter of Lope De Vega travelled kindly in the hands of rider William Buick before being asked to quicken at the furlong marker.

From that point, the response was instantaneous as the 7/4 favourite shot clear of her toiling rivals to score geared down by an enormous seven-and-a-half length margin from Scommessa Sicura and go one better than her mother, Dubai Fountain, who was runner-up in the Group 2 contest.

Bookmakers William Hill reacted by slashing Godolphin's unbeaten filly to 6/1 favourite (from 25/1) for next May's Betfred 1,000 Guineas, while the Leeds-based firm installed Musical Times as 7/4 market leader for the bet365 Fillies' Mile at Newmarket on October 9.

'We'll head to the Fillies' Mile, which was always our plan since Yarmouth really,' reported a delighted Appleby who was saddling his sixth winner from nine September runners.

'She's handled that slightly slower ground today but she's a neat filly, so if it came up quick at Newmarket in the autumn or in the spring it wouldn't worry me.'

Musical Times streaks to victory in the highlight of day one of the St Leger Festival

SAM'S TOP TIPS FOR DAY TWO 2.25 – Final Objective (ew): The talented Pershaada should relish tackling her own age group after taking on the likes of the trail-blazing Bacio in a warm renewal of the Nunthorpe Stakes at York last time. However, the prospect of easy ground will demand a different skillset from the speedy filly and Final Objective could trouble the likely favourite now he drops to the minimum trip for the first time. The selection posted a clear career best in the Group 2 Gimcrack Stakes at York and a strongly-run five furlongs could see him to good effect. 4.45 – Launch Sequence: The application of the first-time cheekpieces and the return to six furlongs could see Launch Sequence power to a first career success in this competitive nursery. A promising debut over course and distance has been followed by two highly promising efforts in decent company with his creditable effort in the Convivial Maiden at York enhanced when the runner-up was placed in Group company next time out. 5.20 - Something Splendid (e/w): It is quite a while since Peter Chapple-Hyam was enjoying Classic success, but the ardent West Bromwich Albion fan has sent out a couple of winners in recent days and Something Splendid is fancied to defy a 5lb penalty for a recent Yarmouth triumph. No doubt buoyed by his beloved team's start to the new Championship season, the Newmarket handler saw the son of Postponed finish runner-up in a division of this corresponding race last year and, although he was later awarded the race when the winner was thrown out, the selection can win this year's renewal under his own volition today.

The Newmarket handler saddled Desert Flower to win the Fillies' Mile before winning the 1,000 Guineas two years ago, but was at pains to point out she was a different model to Musical Times.

'I don't see why she (Musical Times) shouldn't be a Guineas filly. We won this a couple of years ago with Desert Flower, who went on to win the Guineas.

'Funnily enough I see this filly as more of a Guineas filly than Desert Flower, who was big and scopey and unfortunately didn't quite win the Oaks.'

Waardah was another of the fairer sex to shine on Town Moor, comfortably capturing the Group 2 Betfred Park Hill Fillies' Stakes for trainer Owen Burrows and rider Callum Rodriguez.

'We haven't seen a lot of her as she does appreciate a bit of juice in the ground,' said Burrows.

'It was a good run at Carlisle against David O'Meara's Group 1 filly (Estrange) and she was only beaten a neck at Goodwood on quick ground last time, so I was hopeful today.

'She's in the fillies' race (Prix de Royallieu) in France on Arc weekend so that would be her next target and, depending on how that went, we'd have a look at the Group 1 Fillies & Mares on British Champions Day at Ascot.'

Sports.title: Premier League stars obsessed with collecting football cards in their free time
Sports.content:
Premier League stars obsessed with collecting football cards in their free time

Crystal Palace and England midfielder Adam Wharton sold his Topps card collection earlier this year for over £2,000 to YouTuber Jack White

View 3 Images Adam Wharton with YouTuber Jack White (GBW)

Premier League players are taking their obsession for the sport to the next level - by collecting football cards.

‌



In their downtime away from playing and training, big names such as Declan Rice, Dominic Solanke and Tosin Adarabioyo were seen either opening or promoting cards or collectibles. Many footballers even have their own separate trading card Instagram accounts.

‌



One of them is Crystal Palace and England midfielder Adam Wharton, who recently sold his Topps card collection for over £2,000 to YouTuber Jack White. Jack, 26, who runs the GBW account and is from Kent, has been collecting stickers or cards for the last 20 years and now has over 200,000 YouTube subscribers and over 100,000 followers on Tiktok.

‌



He said: "I started collecting while in primary school aged 5/6 and then that progressed into Match Attax from the very first collection. I started filming myself open packs when I was 12 while at secondary school, so been going ever since."

3 View 3 Images Jack's favourite is the Messi Argentina 100 club 101 card 3 View 3 Images Jack says the 1/1 Autographed Clive Tyldesley is his most valuable

‌



When asked which of his prized cards is his favourite, Jack said: "My most valuable would be the 1/1 autographed Clive Tyldesley from Topps UCC Decades 90s Edition which came out in 2025. But my favourite is the Messi Argentina 100 club 101 card which graded a PSA 8 and is one for the collection forever. It's topical too now with his recent retirement."

Jack is not only a massive collector but he's also one of the UK's top content creators for card collectibles. He was keen to offer footy mad youngsters tips on getting into the profession. He said: "My best advice would be to block out the outside noise. Because when I started I had people telling me to stop because cards were deemed ‘not cool’ back then.

"Focus on showing off your passion and an audience will follow. People watch and like GBW because of the longevity perhaps, I’ve got a good personality on camera which I think shines through, not sure! That’s one for my audience to tell me. But this hobby is massive now because of the likes of Match Attax and now new hobby sets with big names starting to collect like the sidemen."

‌



Benjamin Hobart, the Managing Director of SideCards, said: "Over the past few years, we've seen more and more footballers publicly show their interest in collecting. Players like Eden Hazard have been very open about collecting with their children, while Declan Rice has filmed pack-opening videos with members of the Sidemen. Then you have the next generation coming through, with players like JJ Gabriel joining us for a break to celebrate the launch of his first-ever set, Topps Flagship, earlier this year.

"At SideCards, we have personally been lucky to break products with some of the biggest names in the sporting world and, more often than not, once they start ripping packs, it's pretty hard to get them to stop! They get exactly the same buzz we all do from opening a product and hunting for the big chase cards, especially when they're actually in the set themselves."

Lewis Hamilton has recently ventured into the hobby in a commercial capacity, opening his first store in Frankfurt, Germany. Benjamin added: "While seeing players embrace the hobby so publicly still feels relatively new in the UK, the relationship between professional athletes and collectables is already far more established in the US. It feels like athletes in the UK are now starting to follow the same path, with the players themselves becoming collectors, fans of the hobby and, ultimately, an important part of its continued growth."

Article continues below

Match Attax, the UK's original football trading card game, turns 20 this year. Created to celebrate two decades of collecting, swapping and playing, the 20th Anniversary Edition brings a host of serious upgrades for the 2026/27 season. The biggest change comes with an all-new rarity system, with new symbols helping collectors identify cards from Rare, Super-Rare, Mega-Rare, Ultra-Rare, Hyper-Rare through to the ultimate Mystical full-art cards.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick gives Luke Shaw injury update after he misses game before Manchester derby
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick gives Luke Shaw injury update after he misses game before Manchester derby

Luke Shaw was missing from the Manchester United squad for their 4-0 win against Azerbaijani side Sabah on Thursday night and Red Devils boss Michael Carrick has given an update

View 2 Images Luke Shaw was a notable omission vs Sabah (Image: Getty Images)

Michael Carrick has revealed Luke Shaw’s absence against Sabah on Thursday night was just a precaution. The defender was missing from the Red Devils’ squad for their comfortable 4-0 win in their Champions League opener at Old Trafford.

‌



But the United boss has assured fans that he wasn’t ruled out with a serious issue and his absence was just a precautionary measure ahead of this weekend’s derby clash with local rivals Manchester City.

‌



Speaking before Thursday evening’s game, Carrick said: "It's a little bit of that [managing him]. He came off the other day [at Everton] with a little bit of cramp.

‌



“We didn't want to take any risks really. We tried to manage him so we will see how he is after this one."

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



Carrick reshuffled his side in the absence of Shaw, with Patrick Dorgu instead being selected at left-back. The Dane enjoyed a positive evening, having teed up Matheus Cunha for the Red Devils’ opener, while he also managed to help the side to their first clean sheet of the campaign.

He was also named the UEFA Player of the Match. Speaking after United’s emphatic win, Dorgu said: “It was good. Really thank you to god for the giving me the opportunity to play in the Champions League.

“I’m really happy with my performance and really happy that the team got the three points and are up and running in the Champions League.”

‌



He added: “The last couple of games, we conceded a lot of goals so it was good to get the confidence going into the derby at the weekend.”

View 2 Images Patrick Dorgu played a left back for Man United vs Sabah (Image: Getty Images)

Carrick was also able to give Dorgu a rest, with fellow defender Harry Amass handed a late cameo off the bench at left-back, having been left out of the squad for the 2-2 draw with Everton on the weekend.

‌



United boss Carrick was left satisfied with the Red Devils' ability to keep Sabah out. He said: "It's nice to have a clean sheet and obviously win the game. There was a lot. I thought some of our attacking play was fantastic. Some of the football we played was really good, dangerous on transition.

"Defended on the most part really well. I have to give them [Sabah] a lot of credit. A really tough team to play against. They play little connections and make you really work to get the ball back. The result looks comfortable, it wasn't always like that. I thought we did a lot of good things tonight which gave us a good result."

Sports.title: Fenerbahce manager resigns from fourth stint hours after Mason Greenwood decision
Sports.content:
Fenerbahce manager resigns from fourth stint hours after Mason Greenwood decision

Mason Greenwood's manager at Fenerbahce resigned hours after a decision on the Manchester United academy graduate ahead of their first Champions League match for 18 years

View 2 Images Mason Greenwood's Fenerbahce manager has resigned only two months after signing the Manchester United academy graduate (Image: UEFA via Getty Images)

Fenerbahce manager Ismail Kartal announced his resignation during a press conference after their 1-1 draw with Roma in the Champions League. His fourth stint in charge of the Turkish giants ends days after reports that he was giving consideration to playing Mason Greenwood as a second forward.

‌



Marco Asenio's lack of fitness and Matteo Guendouzi being suspended forced Kartal to think outside of the box. However, he ultimately decided against moving the Manchester United academy graduate from the right wing.

‌



Greenwood, 24, assisted their equalising goal, which Archie Brown scored. However, the hosts were ultimately unable to find a winner.

‌



Fenerbahce issue Mason Greenwood statement as UEFA investigate ex-Man Utd star READ MORE :

Man Utd receive explanation from Barcelona for Marcus Rashford transfer snub READ MORE :

In his press conference, Kartal said: "As of this evening, I would like to congratulate my players and announce my resignation from my post." He continued: "I have taken this decision to pave the way for my club.

"I have resigned from my post while there is still time, to assist my beloved Fenerbahce, my players and future managers. I wish everyone a good evening, on the understanding that I shall never return."

This resignation marks the end of his fourth spell in charge of the Turkish giants. He also spent a decade playing for them, winning the league twice.

‌



View 2 Images (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The former defender worked in Fenerbahce's academy for two years after retiring before beginning his managerial career elsewhere. Kartal returned as their assistant coach nine years later, winning two more titles and a pair of Turkish Cups.

‌



After four years in that role, he took over as manager after the incumbent resigned. However, it took just a season before he decided to leave himself after finishing second to Galatasaray and being beaten by Buraspor in the cup semi-finals.

Kartal returned seven years later, replacing the future Nottingham Forest and Wolverhampton Wanderers head coach Vitor Pereira. He again led Fenerbahce to second place.

Kartal delivered a 99-point season; however, Galatasaray managed 102 to win the league, and he left. Then, two years later, Fenerbahce turned to him once again this summer.

Sports.title: Man Utd star JJ Gabriel sparks social media concern after record-breaking hat-trick
Sports.content:
Man Utd star JJ Gabriel sparks social media concern after record-breaking hat-trick

Young Man Utd star JJ Gabriel has drawn plenty of attention for his displays in the club's academy teams and fans will be eager to see him in the first team

View 2 Images JJ Gabriel is one of Man Utd's brightest prospects (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United starlet JJ Gabriel has wiped all images from his Instagram profile. The striker bagged a hat-trick on his UEFA Youth League debut during Thursday's 5-0 thrashing of Sabah FK Under-19s.

‌



Gabriel found the net in the 45th, 85th and 87th minutes to cement his reputation as one of the Red Devils' most promising prospects. He became the youngest-ever player to net a treble for United in the European competition, aged just 15 years and 339 days.

‌



The rising talent has captured supporters' imaginations, generating considerable buzz at Old Trafford. However, the teenager has curiously deleted every photograph from his Instagram account, apparently without offering any reason.

‌



Man Utd batter Sabah to enjoy dream Champions League return - 5 talking points READ MORE :

Man Utd receive explanation from Barcelona for Marcus Rashford transfer snub READ MORE :

Speculation is rife over whether he might break into Michael Carrick's first-team squad for Premier League action this season.

Top-flight rules in English football stipulate that a player must reach 15 on or before August 31 of a particular season to qualify for league selection. This meant he was ineligible to appear in the last campaign, but could now feature in 2026/27.

Should Reds boss Carrick give him an outing before he turns 16 in October, the youngster would become United's youngest-ever first-team player. The Reds' academy players have been given a boost in their bid to break into the first team, with U21 boss Adam Lawrence switching from a 4-3-3 formation to mirror Carrick's 4-2-3-1 system.

‌



View 2 Images JJ Gabriel featured for Manchester United during pre-season (Image: Ash Donelon/Manchester United via Getty Images)

The tactical shift should mean United's youngsters, Gabriel included, arrive in the senior setup with a far clearer grasp of what is expected of them.

The formation change is said to give Gabriel the opportunity to get to grips with Bruno Fernandes' No. 10 role.

‌



Meanwhile, the U21s have replicated Carrick's use of Matheus Cunha as a false nine by deploying Amir Ibragimov in the striker's position.

Sports.title: Baffled Champions League star learns his manager resigned straight after final whistle
Sports.content:
Baffled Champions League star learns his manager resigned straight after final whistle

England youth international Archie Brown was caught up in a storm after learning Fenerbahce boss Ismail Kartal resigned during post-match duties

View 2 Images Archie Brown found out his manager resigned during a post-match interview. (Image: De Marke Sports/X)

Englishman Archie Brown was involved in an awkward mixed zone interview when he found out that Fenerbahce manager Ismail Kartal resigned. The shock decision from the Turkish tactician came in the wake of their 1-1 draw with AS Roma.

‌



The Champions League only kicked off this week but it hasn't been without incident as the resignation looks set to steal the headlines. Kartal stepped down from his post in a bizarre announcement during his post-match press conference in a brutal end to his fourth spell in charge of the Turkish giants.

‌



Brown, who opened the scoring before Bryan Cristante equalised for the Serie A side, was told by the club's media assistant about the news that the manager resigned.

‌



Fenerbahce manager resigns from fourth stint hours after Mason Greenwood decision READ MORE :

The 24-year-old was told: "Ismail Kartal resigned. He said did he make any statement to you?" Brown looks back at the Turkish official with a bemused look and said: "Why do you mean he resigned?

"As what? As coach? What do you mean by resigned? He's not the coach anymore I didn't know about this."

Kartal is in his fourth spell as Fenerbahce coach and had only been appointed as the head coach in June, a third spell at the helm since 2022.

‌



JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

The 65-year-old had spent 10 years at the Istanbul club during his playing career but vowed to never return to the club, he said: “I am resigning from my position while there is still time. I am resigning with the understanding that I will never return.

“I have been here for three months. From the beginning of the season until today, the training sessions and camps I conducted with my players… Our president and managers tried to help us in every way.

‌



“Those were wonderful days. As of this evening, I congratulate my players and I am resigning from my position. Therefore, I would like to thank all my fans, media members, staff, and fellow players who have supported me until today.

“I made this decision to pave the way for my club. We made this decision together as a team.”

View 2 Images Ismail Kartal resigned during his press conference. (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

‌



However, the drama hasn't ended there with club president Aziz Yildrim refusing to accept the resignation. He told press after the game that the decision surprised those within the club, insisting that he will remain at the club.

Yildrim said: “As long as I am here, Ismail Kartal is the head coach. He cannot leave until I leave.”

Brown has been at Fenerbahce since arriving from Gent in 2025. The Birmingham-born defender made the move to Lausanne-Sport after spending his formative years at West Brom then Derby County.

Sports.title: Todd Boehly era at Chelsea nearly over with talks accelerating for duo to sell shares
Sports.content:
Todd Boehly era at Chelsea nearly over with talks accelerating for duo to sell shares

Chelsea's majority owners, Clearlake Capital, are reportedly close to concluding talks to buy the minority stakes held by American businessmen Todd Boehly and Mark Walter

View 2 Images Todd Boehly is close to cashing out at Chelsea (Image: Vince Mignott/Getty Images)

Todd Boehly and Mark Walter are close to cashing out at Chelsea, with Clearlake Capital closing in on a deal to buy their minority stakes.

‌



It emerged last month that Boehly and Walter had entered talks to sell their 12.8 per cent stakes in Chelsea. The American businessmen were part of the BlueCo consortium which purchased the Premier League club from Roman Abramovich in May 2022, ending the Russian oligarch's 19-year spell as owner.

‌



BlueCo paid £2.5billion for the Blues and pledged to invest a further £1.75bn into the club. Chelsea have endured a rollercoaster ride in the subsequent years, with over £1.5bn spent on transfers while tensions have emerged behind the scenes.

‌



Chelsea chairman and co-owner Boehly and Clearlake chief Behdad Eghbali have clashed over plans for the future, including for a possible redevelopment of Stamford Bridge.

FOLLOW OUR CHELSEA FB PAGE! Latest Blues news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

‌



Clearlake is the majority shareholder, holding 61.5 per cent of the club, with the remaining 38.5 per cent is split equally between Walter, Boehly and Swiss billionaire Hansjorg Wyss. The possibility of the shareholders buying each other out has continually arisen over the past few years - and now Clearlake are poised to take control.

Bloomberg reports that a deal is nearly done after talks accelerated in recent weeks. Previous talks have always broken down over price, but a spokesperson for Walter boasted that the 66-year-old will pocket a profit when the deal is completed.

“This potential transaction values Mark Walter’s stake in Chelsea Football Club at a premium to his initial investment and is another successful sports investment for him,” the spokesperson said in a statement to Bloomberg. “After this exit, Mr. Walter intends to make future sports-related investments.

‌



View 2 Images Todd Boehly and fellow co-owner Mark Walter are both selling up to Clearlake (Image: Chris Brunskill/Fantasista/Getty Images)

“Walter did not initiate the proposed transaction to sell his interest, which has been in the works for quite some time."

It remains unclear whether the 90-year-old Wyss wants to cash out, but the move is continuing a theme for Walter, who agreed to sell basketball team Los Angeles Lakers to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger for a record $12.5bn (£9.25bn) last month.

‌



BlueCo's time in charge of Chelsea has seen a massive volume of players traded, with six different permanent managers also coming and going. Now managed by Xabi Alonso, the team spent £349m on transfers this summer, bringing in 11 players while selling 17 for £382m and loaning out 22 to record a profit.

Chelsea sit fourth in the Premier League table, having won two and lost one of their opening three matches. Their new-look attack has proven to be hugely exciting, with their 6-3 comeback win over Leeds in the Carabao Cup showing their potential.

Sports.title: Premier League star admits he would CYCLE to Man Utd after transfer collapse
Sports.content:
Premier League star admits he would CYCLE to Man Utd after transfer collapse

Manchester United chose not to sign a new defender this summer but it appears that a former Bundesliga star would have accepted a move to Old Trafford had he been approached

View 2 Images Thomas Meunier penned a deal with Sunderland this summer (Image: Getty Images)

Sunderland star Thomas Meunier claims he would jump at the chance to sign for Manchester United - but is happy at the Stadium of Light. The Belgian defender joined the Black Cats on a free transfer this summer following his exit from Lille.

‌



A boyhood United fan, Meunier has said that he would have done anything to join the Red Devils, albeit is very happy with the choice he made.

‌



Speaking to Walfoot, the 34-year-old said: “You don’t always get to choose exactly where you want to go. Otherwise, I’d have gone to Bayern Munich, Real Madrid, or Manchester United! But seriously, they [Sunderland] called me and were incredibly convincing.

‌



“Their pitch was good. The conversation with the manager was, too: you spend an hour on the phone talking football, and you realize you’re dealing with a guy who simply loves the game—just like I do.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

‌



“And the fact that it was Sunderland… It just so happens there’s that documentary – Sunderland ‘til I Die – which I really enjoyed.”

On his affection for the Red Devils, the former Dortmund star added: “If they ever ask me, I’ll cycle there. (laughs). But maybe it’s better this way. Suppose I play there and have a bad time. I wouldn’t want to hate Manchester United, because I love that club so much.

“I went to watch them a few weeks ago, against Bilbao. In with the fans, singing, à fond (fully). Je suis un vrai. (I am a real one). I go to watch them at least once every season.

‌



“But of all the home games I’ve seen in all those years, they’ve only won two. You have to have a self cruelty side to be a United supporter, right?”

View 2 Images Thomas Meunier is a boyhood Man United fan (Image: Getty Images)

Ironically, Meunier seemingly had the chance to sign for his boyhood club in the past, only to pass up on the chance due to an unspecified coach encouraging him to sign a deal with his agent first.

‌



Speaking last year, he said: "When I was at Dortmund. I could have signed for Manchester United. I didn’t have an agent. And, in fact, the coach there at the time clearly directed me to his agent so I could sign for Manchester United. I refused, and I didn’t sign. Otherwise, you would have known… But there you go.”

“That’s also the negative side of football," he added. "There’s a lot of money at stake. And even coaches work with agents specifically to place players and get paid. I have 45 examples like that. Now, I can’t prove them all, so I won’t name any names. But it’s something that, in my opinion, still happens far too frequently.”

Sports.title: Premier League plan for £550m boost opposed by 'Big Six' clubs in new financial dispute
Sports.content:
Premier League plan for £550m boost opposed by 'Big Six' clubs in new financial dispute

The Premier League's 'Big Six' - Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United, and Tottenham Hotspur - are reportedly in dispute with the league's other 14 clubs

View 2 Images Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City, Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur are the highest revenue generating Premier League clubs (Image: PA)

Premier League clubs are reportedly in dispute over a proposal to increase revenue from sponsors by collectively selling additional commercial rights.

‌



However, clubs such as Manchester United are said to view any further pooling of rights as an impediment to their aspirations to expand their individual income. The league's 'Big Six' - Arsenal, Chelsea, Liverpool, Manchester City, Man United, and Tottenham Hotspur Hotspur - apparently oppose the proposition.

‌



They are the clubs currently generating the highest revenues, all now exceeding £490million. Aston Villa and Newcastle United are the only clubs that currently come close. However, their 2024/25 incomes were between £300-400million.

‌



Man Utd, Arsenal and Liverpool learn fate as Premier League announce Christmas schedule READ MORE :

Premier League responds after Mauricio Pochettino calls for Chelsea to be stripped of title READ MORE :

The Telegraph reports that the Premier League believes they could increase their annual commercial revenue from £200m to £750m. That would be done by adding rights inventory to the total package offered to sponsors, such as match-day perimeter LED boards.

They currently collectively sell some perimeter advertising, which is shared equally among all 20 clubs as central payments. However, the majority is sold individually by clubs.

'Big Six' clubs would reportedly want a greater share if any expanded commercial offering does pass. The report cites Premier League sources who say they are working with clubs to agree on a solution.

‌



View 2 Images Clubs such as Sir Jim Ratcliffe's Manchester United are said to be opposing the Premier League proposal (Image: Ash Donelon, Manchester United via Getty Images)

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

All clubs are said to have held detailed discussions about the issue twice already this year, first in February and then at June's AGM. It is expected that these rights will be addressed at a league shareholders' meeting on September 24.

‌



Changes to the league's rulebook require at least 14 clubs to vote in favour. For example, six clubs opposed this season's new squad cost ratio (SCR) rules, but the quorum overruled them.

However, they were not the 'Big Six' back then. That sextet were said to be Bournemouth, Brentford, Brighton & Hove Albion, Crystal Palace, Fulham and Leeds United.

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
